title: Sergeant Patrick Kelly - SMP

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
NOV 25 1939

Kelly Given
Clean Slate
By Council

Full Remuneration Is
Settled On S.M.P.
Sergeant

Acting on the instructions
handed down by the Court of
Consuls, the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council yesterday recon-
sidered its action taken last
spring in summarily dismiss-
ing Sergeant Patrick Kelly, of
of the S.M.P., by cancelling
the order for his dismissal.
In cancelling the order, the
S.M.C. automatically gave Ser-
geant Kelly a clean slate and at
the same time restored his rights
regarding payment of superan-
nuation, passage money, back
salary and subsistence allowance
as well as minor allowances.
Besides receiving his superannua-
tion, said to amount to approxima-
tely £500, Sergeant Kelly is being
given six months pay in lieu of
notice, THE CHINA PRESS was in-
formed last night.

Subsistence Allowance

He will also receive a subsistence
allowance equal to his pay for the
months that followed his discharge
up to Monday of this week when
the Court of Consuls rendered judg-
ment against the S.M.C. after the
sergeant had brought action, charg-
ing wrongful dismissal.
In addition to allowances and his
superannuation, Sergeant Kelly
also will receive passage money back
to England, according to informa-
tion in the hands of THE CHINA
PRESS.

Case Recalled

Sergeant Kelly was dismissed
from the police force last May
following a hearing before an
S.M.P. trial officer in accordance
with S.M.C. rules and regula-
tions. The discharge, based on
three minor infractions of
S.M.P. regulations and one grave
charge alleging failure to report the
seizure of a pistol and opium, dis-
honored the sergeant and caused
something of a sensation in police
circles. The case was finally given
a public airing when Sergeant Kelly
brought action against the S.M.C.
in the Court of Consuls, charging
that he had been wrongfully dis-
missed. The Court, in rendering
judgment, stated that the punish-
ment in the case of the first three
charges was excessive and threw out
the fourth charge because of lack
of evidence.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）
1939年11月25日

凯利获
清白记录
由公董局给予

全额薪酬
已就上海公共租界工部局警务处
巡长一事达成结算

遵照领事法庭下达的指令，上海公共租界工部局昨日重新审议了今年春季对上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）巡长帕特里克·凯利（Patrick Kelly）作出的即决开除处分，并撤销了该开除令。
在撤销该命令时，工部局自动为凯利巡长恢复了清白记录，同时恢复了他领取养老金、遣返费、欠薪及生活津贴以及其他小额津贴的权利。
据《字林西报》昨晚获悉，除了领取据说约为500英镑的养老金外，凯利巡长还将获得相当于六个月薪金的代通知金。

生活津贴

他还将获得一笔生活津贴，金额等于其被解雇后至本周一期间（即领事法庭在该巡长提起诉讼指控非法解雇并对工部局作出判决之时）的薪金。
除各项津贴和养老金外，据《字林西报》掌握的消息，凯利巡长还将获得返回英国的遣返费。

案件回顾

去年五月，根据工部局的规章制度，凯利巡长在上海公共租界工部局警务处审判官举行的听证会后被警队开除。此次解雇基于三项轻微违反警务处规定的行为，以及一项严重指控，指称其未报告缴获手枪和鸦片一事，这使该巡长蒙受耻辱，并在警界引起了一定轰动。当凯利巡长在领事法庭对工部局提起诉讼，指控其被非法解雇时，此案最终得以公开审理。法庭在作出判决时表示，针对前三项指控的处罚过重，并因证据不足驳回了第四项指控。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY
No. S. P. D.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY

NOV 21 1939

Delighted

Not Surprised
Winner of one of the most important and far-reaching legal decisions ever handed down in Shanghai, Mr. Kelly did not appear to be too greatly surprised that he won the case from the SMC.
Mr. Kelly declared that throughout the long months of waiting his problems had been made all the easier and comforting by the kindness of many comrades on the police force, and the untiring zeal which Mr. Henry A. Reeks, his counsel, had devoted to the case.

Regrets
"Leaving the many comrades I have found in Shanghai in the 10 years that I have been here, will be my deepest regret," Kelly said to the Evening Post reporter. "In fact," he added, "when the time actually comes for me to leave I shall probably have to rush away suddenly without warning any of them."
"They have been great to me," Kelly declared in referring to friends of his in the SMP. "They have helped me in many ways and I shall always be grateful."

Lawyer Thanked
"I know that Mr. Reeks has worked very hard on my behalf and I deeply appreciate all the splendid things he has done," Mr. Kelly declared.
Speaking of the court hearings, he said: "Even if I had lost the case I would have been satisfied, because I knew right from the beginning that I was getting a fair hearing. I knew that because Mr. Gauss, the American Consul-General, asked questions frequently and made me explain a few details."

Ten Years In SMP
Mr. Kelly was born in Carlisle (five miles from Gretna Green) on March 17, 1905, and studied at St. Patrick's school. His father, who died only last year, had served previously with the British army for nearly 32 years, and during the World War had been decorated with the Distinguished Conduct Medal.
After leaving school, Mr. Kelly joined the L.M.S. Railway and served with it until 1929, when he enrolled in the SMPolice, arriving here on November 11 of the same year.
Within a few years Kelly was attached to the C.I.D. and among his achievements in this branch of the force was the arrest last December of a gang of 53 burglars, third largest ever to be apprehended within the Settlement.

Winner Of SMC Claim
P. J. Kelly Plans
Xmas At Home

Aid Of SMP Comrades
In Past Months
Appreciated

"I want to be home....in England....with my wife and two children....for Christmas...."
Behind the deep sentiment of the words stood the story of six months of anxiety which had at last been overcome, for the words were spoken by Mr. Patrick John Kelly to a reporter of the Shanghai Evening Post a few hours after the former member of the Shanghai Municipal Police had received the announcement of the victory awarded him by the Court of Consuls, in his suit against the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Mr. Kelly told the Evening Post that now he was only waiting to hear the decision of the SMC. After this, he said, he would try to reach England as fast as he could, and join his wife and children, for whom he had been able to obtain third class passage and send home last August.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. M. 登记处
编号 S. P. D.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）

1939年11月21日

欣喜

并不惊讶
作为上海有史以来最重要且影响最深远的法律判决之一的胜诉方，凯利先生对于自己赢得针对工部局（SMC）的诉讼似乎并未感到过于惊讶。
凯利先生表示，在漫长的等待岁月中，警队中许多同僚的善意，以及他的律师亨利·A·里克斯（Henry A. Reeks）先生为本案投入的不懈热情，使他的困境变得更容易承受并倍感慰藉。

遗憾
“离开我在上海这十年间结识的众多同僚，将是我最大的遗憾，”凯利对《晚邮报》记者说。“事实上，”他补充道，“当真正离别的时刻到来时，我可能不得不突然匆匆离去，无法提前告知他们任何人。”
“他们对我非常好，”凯利在提及他在上海公共租界工部局警务处（SMP）的朋友时宣称。“他们在许多方面帮助了我，我将永远感激。”

感谢律师
“我知道里克斯先生为我非常努力地工作，我深深感激他所做的一切出色工作，”凯利先生宣称。
谈及法庭听证会时，他说：“即使我输掉了官司，我也会感到满意，因为我从一开始就知道我得到了公正的聆讯。我之所以知道这一点，是因为美国总领事高斯（Gauss）先生频繁提问，并要求我解释一些细节。”

在上海公共租界工部局警务处任职十年
凯利先生于1905年3月17日出生于卡莱尔（Carlisle，距格雷特纳格林Gretna Green五英里），曾在圣帕特里克学校（St. Patrick's school）就读。他的父亲于去年去世，此前曾在英国军队服役近32年，并在世界大战期间荣获杰出服务勋章（Distinguished Conduct Medal）。
毕业后，凯利先生加入了伦敦、米德兰和苏格兰铁路公司（L.M.S. Railway），并在此工作至1929年，同年他加入上海公共租界工部局警务处（SMPolice），于当年11月11日抵达上海。
几年内，凯利被调至刑事侦缉处（C.I.D.），他在该部门取得的成就包括去年十二月逮捕了一个由53名窃贼组成的团伙，这是租界内有史以来被捕人数第三多的团伙。

赢得对工部局的索赔
P. J. 凯利计划
回家过圣诞节

感激过去数月
上海公共租界工部局警务处同僚的
援助

“我想回家……回英国……和我的妻子及两个孩子一起……过圣诞节……”
在这句话深沉的情感背后，是一段长达六个月的焦虑故事，而这段焦虑终于得以克服。说这话的是帕特里克·约翰·凯利（Patrick John Kelly）先生，他在前上海公共租界工部局警务处成员收到领事法庭在其起诉上海公共租界工部局一案中判其胜诉的通知几小时后，对《上海晚邮报》的一名记者说了这番话。
凯利先生告诉《晚邮报》，现在他只是在等待工部局的决定。他说，此后他将尽快设法前往英国，与他的妻儿团聚；他已于去年八月为他们办妥了三等舱船票并送他们回国。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
NOV 20 1939
No. S. P. D. 471

SMP Dismissal Grounds
For Kelly Held Wrong

Council Ordered
To Alter Basis
For Payments

Stigma Of SMP Action
Ordered Expunged
By Consuls

SUCCESS GAINED
BY H. A. REEKS

Ex-Sergeant Of Police
Wins Substantial
Part Of Claim

“If You Knock The “L”
Out Of Kelly, He’ll Knock The
“I” Out Of You”—old song.)

In one of the most important legal decisions ever handed down in Shanghai, P. J. Kelly, former member of the Shanghai Municipal Police, was awarded judgment with full court costs and attorney’s fees in his suit against the Shanghai Municipal Council for wrongful dismissal, in the judgment reached this morning by the Court of Consuls.

The judgment set aside the fourth charge made against Kelly which led to his dismissal by the SMPolice, as being circumstantial at best,” while the other three charges were declared by the Court as “unjustified in bringing about a serious penalty and the stigma imposed on Kelly by the Council in its order of dismissal.”

All Not Granted

Total claim sought by Kelly in his suit against the Council in connection with his petition that he had wrongfully been dismissed, were 500 pounds sterling which he declared to be due him under the Council’s superannuation scheme, $3546, representing six months’ salary, and money for passages for his wife and two children to return to England.

The judgment handed down this morning by the Court of Consuls, although not granting Kelly’s claims entirely, states that “the cause is remanded to the Council for reconsideration with a view to such alternation and modification of the judgment of punishment as will be commensurate with and justified by the findings of the first three charges.

Police Charges

Major importance of the judgment rendered by the Court of Consuls, can be attached to the following passage contained in the document:

“This Court,” the judgment reads, “has very carefully examined the police charges made against the petitioner Kelly, and the evidence in the case as shown by the record. It has carefully weighed the arguments of counsel, and in reaching its decision it has sought to do substantial and basic justice, not alone by way of assuring the protection of the rights of the petitioner Kelly as an individual, but also from the viewpoint that adequate and effective powers must be lodged in and maintained by the Council in its exercise of disciplinary control over the conduct and administration of its police force.”

Misconduct Claim

Pointing out the petitioner’s claims filed against the SMC, the judgment declares that Kelly brought action for wrongful dismissal from the police force on May 1, the dismissal having been based by the SMF Police on four charges of misconduct by Kelly of police regulations.

The charges against Kelly also included several Chinese members of the police force, and declared that the group had extorted money from the Chinese occupant of a house on Taku Road.

Technical Violations

With regard to these charges against Kelly, the judgment by the Court of Consuls declares: “It remains to be seen whether the proceedings as conducted by the officers of the Council in the instant case conform to and faithfully observe the Rules and Regulations under which the petitioner Kelly was charged and dismissed from the police force.”

The first three charges, to which Kelly admitted guilt, “the Court considers were based upon technical violations of the Rules and Regulations governing the conduct of police officers,” the judgment adds, and then points out that “there might be reason to doubt whether the charges against Kelly were supported by the preponderance of the evidence. The Court is of the opinion that had the first three charges been the only charges pending against Kelly, and had there been no injection of outside and extraneous issues, Kelly would in all probability merely have been subjected to comparatively moderate disciplinary measures. The first, second and third charges are not in essence, culpable offenses, and the Court believes that, standing alone, they could not have justified or supported the serious and grave penalty—and the stigma—imposed on the petitioner Kelly by the Council in its order of dismissal.”

Reeks The Winner

Mr. Henry Arthur Reeks, “the winner,” of Messrs. Ellis and Hays, prosecuted at the hearings on behalf of the petitioner, P. J. Kelly, while Mr. R. T. Bryan, Jr., represented the SMC.

Hearings were held before Consular Judges, with Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, U. S. Consul-General presiding, supported by Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-General, and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General, with Mr. E. A. Long taking part as Special Commissioner.

D.C. Sp 131
C 99

《上海晚邮报与信使报》
1939年11月20日
编号 S. P. D. 471

认定工部局警务处
解雇凯利的理由不当

命令公董局
更改支付
依据

领事命令
抹去工部局警务处行动
带来的污名

H. A. 里克斯
获得成功

前警员
赢得索赔的
实质性部分

“如果你把凯利（Kelly）名字里的‘L’去掉，他就会把你名字里的‘I’去掉”——老歌歌词。）

在上海有史以来最重要的法律判决之一中，前上海公共租界工部局警务处成员 P. J. 凯利在起诉上海公共租界工部局非法解雇一案中，获领事法庭今晨作出的判决支持，赢得全部诉讼费用及律师费。

该判决撤销了导致凯利被上海公共租界工部局警务处解雇的第四项指控，认为该指控“充其量只是间接证据”，而法院宣布其余三项指控“不足以引发严厉处罚，也不足以证明工部局在其开除令中对凯利施加的污名是正当的”。

并非全部获准

凯利在与工部局的诉讼中提出的索赔总额包括：他声称根据工部局养老金计划应得的500英镑；代表六个月薪金的3,546美元；以及其妻子和两个孩子返回英国的船费。

领事法庭今晨下达的判决虽然未完全支持凯利的诉求，但指出“本案发回工部局重新审议，以便根据前三项指控的调查结果，对处罚判决进行相称且正当的调整和修改。”

警方指控

领事法庭所作判决的重要性，可体现在文件中所含的以下段落：

判决书写道：“本庭非常仔细地审查了针对申请人凯利提出的警方指控，以及记录所示的案件证据。本庭仔细权衡了双方律师的辩论，并在作出决定时力求实现实质性和基本的正义，这不仅是为了确保保护申请人凯利作为个人的权利，也是从这样的观点出发：工部局在对其警队的行为和行政行使纪律控制权时，必须拥有并保持充分且有效的权力。”

不当行为指控

判决指出申请人针对工部局提交的诉求，声明凯利于5月1日就非法被警队解雇一事提起诉讼，该解雇是上海公共租界工部局警务处基于凯利违反警务规定的四项不当行为指控而作出的。

针对凯利的指控还涉及几名华籍警员，并称该团伙向大沽路（Taku Road）一处房屋的华人住户勒索钱财。

技术性违规

关于针对凯利的这些指控，领事法庭的判决声明：“尚待查明工部局官员在本案中进行的程序是否符合并忠实遵守了据以指控申请人凯利并将其从警队开除的规则和条例。”

判决补充道，对于凯利承认有罪的前三项指控，“法院认为这些指控是基于对管辖警员行为的规则和条例的技术性违反”，并随后指出“有理由怀疑针对凯利的指控是否得到优势证据的支持。法院认为，如果仅有前三项指控悬而未决，且没有引入外部和无关的问题，凯利很可能只会受到相对适度的纪律处分。第一、第二和第三项指控本质上并非应受谴责的罪行，法院认为，仅凭这些指控本身，不足以证明或支持工部局在其开除令中对申请人凯利施加的严厉且严重的惩罚——以及污名。”

里克斯获胜

埃利斯和海斯律师事务所（Messrs. Ellis and Hays）的亨利·阿瑟·里克斯（Henry Arthur Reeks）先生作为“胜诉方”，在听证会上代表申请人 P. J. 凯利进行起诉，而 R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan, Jr.）先生则代表工部局。

听证会在领事法官面前举行，由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）先生主持，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯（Herbert Phillips）爵士和日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）先生陪同，E. A. 朗（E. A. Long）先生作为特别委员参与。

D.C. Sp 131
C 99
已归档

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. B. REGISTRY
Council's Decision Set Aside.
By Court of Consuls
Former Police Sergeant's 'Appeal Against Wrongful
Dismissal Upheld ; Question of Severity

A DECISION of the Shanghai Municipal Council by which Patrick
J. Kelly, former British detective-sergeant attached to Central
Police Station, was dismissed from the Force, was set aside yes-
terday by a judgment of the Court of Consuls. Kelly had pre-
viously appeared in an action against the Council when he claimed
that he had been wrongfully dismissed. He asked that the Council
should pay him a sum of £500, which was the amount standing
to his credit in the superannuation fund, and he alleged that he
had been wrongfully deprived of this sum. He further claimed
$3,546, representing six months' pay, his own, his wife's and his
children's second class passage money to England, court fees and
$500.

Kelly was found guilty on four
charges while in the police force
and was dismissed on account of this.
By the decision of the Court of Con-
suls yesterday the judgment of dis-
missal, based on the finding of guilty
on all four charges, was set aside,
while the findings on the fourth
charge were also set aside. The cause
was recommended to the Council for
reconsideration with a view to such
alteration and modification of the
judgment of punishment as would be
commensurate with and justified by
the findings on the first three charges.
Court costs and attorney's fees were
assessed against the Council.

The charges on which Kelly was
found guilty were that he had know-
ingly made and signed a false state-
ment in an official document, the
First Crime Diary, P.I.R. 821; that
he had unnecessarily detained one
Chinese and had released him in an
improper manner; that on March 30,
at Central Station, he had made a
false and untrue statement in his
detective's diary book; and that he
had failed to account for money,
pistol and ammunition and opium
taken at House 7, Lane 182, Taku
Road. The case was heard by Mr.
C. E. Gauss, U.S. Consul-General; Sir
Herbert Phillips, H.M. Consul-Gen-
eral; Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-
General. Mr. H. A. Reeks appeared
on behalf of Kelly, while Mr. R. T.
Bryan, jun., represented the Council.

Judgment

The judgment was as follows: The
petitioner in this case alleges for
cause of action against the Shanghai
Municipal Council that he has been
wrongfully dismissed from the police
force of the Council and deprived of
certain financial benefits which had
accrued to him during the course of
and as a part of his employment.

It appears that the petitioner en-
tered into a contract of employment
in the police force of the Council,
that he duly entered upon the per-
formance of his duties under the
terms of his employment, and con-
tinued in such employment until May
1, 1939, on which date he was dis-
missed by the Council. This dismissal
appears to have based upon certain
charges preferred against him within
the framework of the Rules and Re-
gulations governing the Conduct of
Police Officers of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council, adopted March 15, 1930,
setting forth the procedure and dis-
ciplinary measures to be taken in
cases of misconduct or other offences
against the said Rules and Regula-
tions. The petitioner alleges that the
hearing of the charges against him
was conducted by the officers of the
Council in an unfair and prejudicial
manner, and that as a result he was
summarily and wrongfully dismissed
from the police force as a dishonest
and unreliable man.

The defendant Council maintains,
in brief, that the charges preferred
against the petitioner Kelly were well
brought and were substantiated by
the testimony taken in the hearing
thereof before the police trial officer;
that the proceedings were conducted
in accordance with the rules of pro-
cedure as laid down in the Rules and
Regulations, in a fair and impartial
manner, and in no way prejudicial
to his rights; that the evidence pre-
sented at the hearing and in supple-
mentary proceedings demonstrates
and proves beyond doubt that the
petitioner, in addition to having
violated certain prescribed Rules and
Regulations, had shown himself to
be thoroughly dishonest and unreli-
able, and not a man who could pro-
perly be continued in employment as
a member of the Shanghai Municipal
Police.

Extortion Charges

It appears that at the same time
that certain charges were preferred
against the petitioner Kelly as a
member of the police force, similar
and additional charges were brought
against several Chinese members of
the force, the substance of the ad-
ditional charges against the last men-
tioned members of the force being
that they extorted money from the
Chinese occupant of a house on Taku
Road. The theory of the Council's
proceedings against the several police
officers is that in connection with the
arrest of a certain Chinese for pos-
session of opium there was evolved
amongst certain police officers con-
cerned a plan to extort money from
the occupant of the house on Taku
Road under threats of arrest if he
did not comply with their demands.
The several charges against the police
officers concerned were heard by the
police trial officer jointly and at the
same hearing. Specifically, the fourth
charge against Kelly was heard in
conjunction with the fifth and sixth
charges against the other officers con-
cerned. Kelly was not named in the
fifth and sixth charges. The evidence
taken in the joint hearing is said by
the defendant Council to justify the
findings on the several charges
against the respective police officer
defendants.

This Court has very carefully
examined the charges made against
the petitioner Kelly, and the evidence
in the case as shown by the record.
It has carefully weighed the argu-
ments of counsel, and in reaching its
decision it has sought to do substan-
tial and basic justice, not alone by
way of assuring the protection of the
rights of the petitioner Kelly as an
individual, but also from the view-
point that adequate and effective
powers must be lodged in and main-
tained by the Council in its exercise
of disciplinary control over the con-
duct and administration of its police
force.

《字林西报》。
上海工部局
S. B. 登记处
领事法庭撤销工部局之决定。
前警佐就“不当解雇”提出上诉获支持；量刑轻重问题

上海工部局此前作出的一项决定，将隶属于中央捕房的英籍侦探警佐帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）从警务处除名，该决定昨日被领事法庭的判决予以撤销。凯利此前曾就控告工部局一案出庭，声称自己遭到不当解雇。他要求工部局支付其养老金账户中结存的500英镑，并指称自己被不当剥夺了这笔款项。他还索赔3,546美元，包括六个月薪水、本人及妻儿返回英国的二等舱船费、诉讼费以及500美元。

凯利在警务处任职期间被裁定四项指控成立，并因此被解职。根据领事法庭昨日的判决，基于全部四项指控成立而作出的解职判决被撤销，同时关于第四项指控的裁定也被撤销。该案被发回工部局重新审议，以便根据前三项指控的裁定结果，对处罚判决进行相称且合理的调整与修改。诉讼费用及律师费由工部局承担。

凯利被裁定成立的指控包括：他在官方文件《第一犯罪日记》（First Crime Diary），P.I.R. 821号中，明知故犯地制作并签署了一份虚假陈述；他不必要地拘留了一名华人，并以不当方式将其释放；3月30日，在中央捕房，他在其侦探日记簿中作了虚假且不实的陈述；以及他未能对在大沽路182弄7号查获的现金、手枪、弹药和鸦片作出交代。本案由美国总领事高斯（C. E. Gauss）先生、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯（Herbert Phillips）爵士、日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）先生审理。H. A. Reeks 先生代表凯利出庭，R. T. Bryan  junior 先生代表工部局。

判决

判决如下：本案申请人诉称，针对上海工部局的诉讼理由是他被不当从工部局警务处解职，并被剥夺了在受雇期间及作为雇佣关系一部分所累积的某些经济利益。

事实显示，申请人与工部局警务处签订了雇佣合同，他依照雇佣条款正式履行职责，并持续受雇至1939年5月1日，当日他被工部局解职。此次解职似乎是基于根据1930年3月15日通过的《上海工部局警务人员行为守则与条例》框架内对他提出的若干指控，该守则与条例规定了在发生 misconduct（行为不端）或违反上述守则与条例的其他罪行时应采取的程序和纪律措施。申请人指称，工部局官员以不公平且带有偏见的方式审理了对他的指控，导致他作为一名不诚实且不可靠的人员被即刻且不当从警务处解职。

被告工部局简要辩称，对申请人凯利提出的指控依据充分，并由警务审判官在听证会上取得的证词所证实；诉讼程序按照《守则与条例》规定的程序规则，以公平、公正的方式进行，并未损害其权利；听证会及补充程序中提交的证据毫无疑问地表明并证明，申请人除了违反某些规定的《守则与条例》外，还表现出彻底的不诚实和不可靠，不适合继续作为上海公共租界警务处的一员受雇。

勒索指控

事实显示，在对身为警务处成员的申请人凯利提出某些指控的同时，也对警务处的几名华籍成员提出了类似及额外的指控，针对后述警务处成员的额外指控实质上是他们向大沽路一处房屋的华人住户勒索钱财。工部局对几名警务官员提起诉讼的理论依据是，在逮捕一名因持有鸦片而被控的特定华人时，涉案的某些警务官员之间酝酿出一个计划，即如果该房屋住户不满足他们的要求，就以逮捕相威胁，向其勒索钱财。对相关警务官员的多项指控由警务审判官合并并在同一次听证会上审理。具体而言，针对凯利的第四项指控是与针对其他相关官员的第五和第六项指控一并审理的。凯利并未在第五和第六项指控中被点名。被告工部局称，合并听证中取得的证据足以证明对各位警务官员被告各项指控的裁定。

本庭非常仔细地审查了针对申请人凯利的指控，以及案卷记录所示的案件证据。本庭仔细权衡了双方律师的辩论意见，在作出裁决时，力求实现实质性和基本的正义，这不仅是为了确保保护申请人凯利作为个人的权利，也是从以下观点出发：工部局在对其警务处的行为和行政行使纪律控制权时，必须拥有并保持充分且有效的权力。

Right of Employer
The petitioner Kelly entered into the performance of his duties under the terms of his contract of employment by the Council which set forth and enumerated his functions and, in a general sense, by its nature, contemplated the performance thereof in a manner satisfactory to the Council and consistent with the rules of conduct as prescribed by administrative regulations adopted from time to time by the Council or its officers.

The Court agrees with the contention of the Council that inherent in a contract of employment is the right of the employer to discharge the employee. Such discharge may be with or without cause unless the circumstances disclose that such absolute and basic right to discharge has been limited, or restricted, or regulated, by adopted rules and regulations which have been either expressly or by construction incorporated in and made a part of the contract of employment. In such case—and it is believed that the employment under consideration falls within such classification—it may not be asserted that the employer still enjoys an absolute right and power of discharge. The employer has voluntarily relinquished certain elements of such power, and has agreed by implication in the contract that he will be bound to exercise his power of discharge only in accordance with and under the terms of the rules and regulations adopted.

Conflict in Testimony
The Court is confident here that the Council's power to discharge a police officer is controlled and regulated by the substantive and procedural provisions laid down and promulgated in the Rules and Regulations of March 15, 1930, and that disciplinary measures taken by the Council must be in accordance with the principles set forth in such Rules and Regulations.
It remains to be seen, therefore, whether the proceedings as conducted by the officers of the Council in the instant case conform to and faithfully observe the Rules and Regulations under which the petitioner Kelly was charged and was dismissed from the police force.
With reference to the first three listed charges against petitioner Kelly, which the Court considers were based upon technical violations of the Rules and Regulations Governing the Conduct of Police Officers, the petitioner Kelly has acknowledged that he is guilty of the act upon which the first listed charge is based, namely, his failure to note in his Crime Diary his visit to Taku Road; but he denies that such omission was made wilfully or with evil intent. In the second and third charges the record discloses substantial conflict in the testimony and there might be reason to doubt whether the charges against Kelly were supported by the preponderance of the evidence.

Moderate Disciplinary Measures
The Court is of the opinion that had the first three charges been the only charges pending against Kelly, and had there been no injection of outside and extraneous issues, Kelly would in all probability merely have been subjected to comparatively moderate disciplinary measures. The first, second and third charges are not in essence, culpable offences, and the Court believes that, standing alone, they could not have justified or supported the serious and grave penalty —and the stigma—imposed on the petitioner Kelly by the Council in its order of dismissal. The Council, however, is not disposed to set aside or fact on the trial officer's findings of does find, and therefore adjudges, that the penalty imposed in the police trial of Kelly is excessive.
The fourth charge against the petitioner Kelly is much graver in aspect; but here it appears that the testimony was highly conflicting, and the procedural as well as the substantive rights of the petitioner Kelly were so obviously prejudiced that the Court has no alternative but to set aside the findings on this charge for the reasons set forth hereafter.
The evidence offered against Kelly in support of this fourth charge is circumstantial at best; the "corpus delicti" is not established; the testimony is conflicting and highly contradictory; and there has not been presented evidence which satisfactorily establishes the probability that Kelly was guilty of the offence charged. This charge against Kelly was heard in conjunction with other charges against other police officer defendants. Kelly was not charged with being implicated in the offences charged against the other police officers concerned. The trial officer in hearing the fourth charge against Kelly along with the fifth and sixth charges against other police officers has permitted the injection of extraneous issues and the admission of incompetent evidence such as could not but influence an ordinary man in his consideration as an impartial judge of the fourth charge against the petitioner Kelly. Such action was prejudicial to the rights of the petitioner Kelly and alone might constitute error such as would necessitate sending the case back for a new hearing. But in addition, this Court is far from satisfied with the evidence offered to establish that a pistol was in fact, found at the house on Taku Road. The only "direct" evidence, if such it may be called, on this point, is that a Chinese prisoner stated that he "overheard" one Chinese detective tell another Chinese detective that a certain paper bag contained a pistol. This "evidence" however was contradicted by the wife of the occupant of the house on Taku Road who admitted that a permit for a pistol was in the house, but denied that the pistol itself was there. The original complaint of extortion inaugurating the police disciplinary proceedings against Kelly and certain Chinese police officers was made by the occupant of this house who, however, did not later appear at the hearing.

Severe Penalty
The Court is unable, on the basis of the record before it, to accept the Council's contention that petitioner Kelly, on the fourth charge, was tried solely on the issues framed therein; that only competent evidence was considered by the trial officer in arriving at his findings on this charge; that the punishment or penalty as ultimately imposed was not affected or influenced by other evidence and issues; and that petitioner Kelly suffered no prejudice or denial of justice thereby. The Court cannot but feel that in the findings returned by the police trial officer and in the judgment of dismissal as entered by the Commissioner of Police and later sustained by the Council on appeal, the dominating factor and influence affecting the minds of the officers and officials concerned in arriving at their respective decisions was that the case, taken as a whole, convinced them that the petitioner Kelly was implicated in and a party to the extortion with which other police officers were charged and found guilty. The thread of extortion runs unfailingly throughout the whole proceedings; it has been injected into the evidence and the issues; it alone could have resulted in the imposition of such a severe penalty as that visited upon petitioner Kelly. But Kelly was not charged with being implicated in or being a party to the extortion, and it cannot be held now that a suspicion that he may have been so implicated justifies the judgment of dismissal as entered. If the extortion was to have been considered in arriving at the punishment or penalty to be imposed, the petitioner Kelly should have been appropriately charged.

Set Aside
However, the Court realizes that as a result of the charges which were preferred against Kelly, and as a result of the suspicion which may have been aroused in the minds of his superior officers that he was involved in the extortion (and the Court is not disposed to say that such a suspicion would be entirely unjustified), it is obvious that Kelly's usefulness as a police officer has been greatly impaired and that he no longer enjoys the confidence of his superiors, a confidence that without question is an essential factor in maintaining the morale and discipline of the police force. His contract of employment with the Council may properly be terminated by measures short of the peremptory dismissal with the stigma attaching to him as a result thereof and the loss of the financial benefits to which he is otherwise entitled.
It is ordered and adjudged that the findings on the fourth charge against Patrick John Kelly and the judgment of dismissal entered on the basis of the finding of guilty on all four charges be set aside. The cause is remanded to the Council for reconsideration with a view to such alteration and modification as the judgment of punishment as will be commensurate with and justified by the findings on the first three charges. Court costs and attorney's fees will be assessed against the Council.

雇主的权利

申请人凯利（Kelly）根据工部局与其签订的雇佣合同条款履行其职责，该合同列明并详述了其职能，且就其性质而言，总体上要求其以令工部局满意的方式履行职责，并遵守工部局或其官员不时通过的行政规章所规定的行为准则。

法院同意工部局的主张，即雇佣合同中固有雇主解雇雇员的权利。除非情况表明，这种绝对且基本的解雇权已通过明示或默示方式纳入并成为雇佣合同一部分的既定规章制度受到限制、约束或规范，否则解雇可以有理由，也可以无理由。在这种情况下——并且相信本案所涉雇佣关系属于此类——不能声称雇主仍享有绝对的解雇权和权力。雇主已自愿放弃该权力的某些要素，并在合同中默示同意，其行使解雇权时将仅受限于并依据所通过的规章制度之条款。

证词中的冲突

法院在此确信，工部局解雇警官的权力受1930年3月15日颁布的《规章条例》中规定的实体和程序条款的控制和规范，且工部局采取的纪律措施必须符合该《规章条例》中阐明的原则。

因此，尚需确定的是，在本案中，工部局官员进行的诉讼程序是否符合并忠实遵守了据以指控申请人凯利并将其从警队除名的《规章条例》。

关于针对申请人凯利列出的前三项指控，法院认为这些指控基于对《警官行为管理规章条例》的技术性违反，申请人凯利承认他犯有第一项指控所依据的行为，即未在其《犯罪日记》中记录其前往大沽路（Taku Road）的访问；但他否认这种遗漏是故意或出于恶意所为。在第二和第三项指控中，记录显示证词存在实质性冲突，人们可能有理由怀疑针对凯利的指控是否得到了优势证据的支持。

适度的纪律处分

法院认为，如果前三项指控是针对凯利的唯一待决指控，且没有引入外部和无关的问题，凯利很可能只会受到相对适度的纪律处分。第一、二和三项指控本质上并非应受谴责的罪行，法院认为，单独来看，这些指控不足以证明或支持工部局在其除名命令中对申请人凯利施加的严重且严厉的惩罚——以及随之而来的污名。然而，工部局并不打算撤销审判官的认定，因此裁定，在凯利的警务审判中施加的惩罚过重。

针对申请人凯利的第四项指控在性质上要严重得多；但在此看来，证词高度冲突，且申请人凯利的程序权利以及实体权利显然受到了损害，以至于法院别无选择，只能基于后文所述理由撤销对此项指控的认定。

为支持这第四项指控而提出的针对凯利的证据充其量只是间接证据；“犯罪事实”（corpus delicti）并未确立；证词相互冲突且高度矛盾；且并未提出能令人满意地确立凯利犯有所控罪行可能性的证据。这项针对凯利的指控是与针对其他警官被告的其他指控一并审理的。凯利并未被指控卷入针对其他相关警官的罪行。审判官在审理针对凯利的第四项指控以及针对其他警官的第五和第六项指控时，允许引入无关问题并采纳无资格证据，这些因素不可避免地会影响一个普通人在作为公正法官考量针对申请人凯利的第四项指控时的判断。这种行为损害了申请人凯利的权利，其本身就可能构成错误，从而需要将案件发回重审。此外，本院对旨在证明确实在大沽路那所房子里发现了一支手枪的证据远不满意。关于这一点的唯一“直接”证据（如果可以这样称呼的话）是一名中国囚犯陈述，他“无意中听到”一名中国侦探告诉另一名中国侦探，某个纸袋里装有一支手枪。然而，这一“证据”遭到了大沽路那所房子居住者的妻子的反驳，她承认家里有一支手枪的许可证，但否认手枪本身在那里。引发针对凯利及某些中国警官的警务纪律程序的原始敲诈勒索投诉正是由该房屋的居住者提出的，但该居住者后来并未出席听证会。

严厉惩罚

基于现有的案卷记录，法院无法接受工部局的主张，即申请人凯利在第四项指控上仅就其中框定的问题受审；审判官在就该指控作出认定时仅考虑了有资格的证据；最终施加的惩罚或处罚未受其他证据和问题的影响或干扰；且申请人凯利未因此遭受不公或正义被剥夺。法院不禁感到，在警务审判官作出的认定中，以及在警务处长作出并经工部局在上诉中维持的除名判决中，影响相关官员和职员作出各自决定的主导因素和影响是：整体案情使他们确信申请人凯利卷入并参与了其他警官被指控并被判有罪的敲诈勒索案。敲诈勒索的线索始终贯穿于整个诉讼过程；它被注入到证据和问题中；唯有它才能导致对申请人凯利施加如此严厉的惩罚。但凯利并未被指控卷入或参与敲诈勒索，现在不能认为对他可能卷入的怀疑足以证明已录入的除名判决是正当的。如果在决定施加的惩罚或处罚时要考虑敲诈勒索情节，本应对申请人凯利进行适当的指控。

撤销

然而，法院意识到，由于针对凯利提出的指控，以及由于其上级官员心中可能产生的他卷入敲诈勒索的怀疑（法院并不认为这种怀疑完全毫无根据），显而易见，凯利作为警官的效用已大大受损，他不再享有上级的信任，而这种信任无疑是维持警队士气和纪律的基本因素。可以通过不如断然除名那样严厉的措施适当终止其与工部局的雇佣合同，从而避免由此给他带来的污名以及丧失他原本有权享有的经济利益。

现命令并裁定，撤销针对帕特里克·约翰·凯利（Patrick John Kelly）第四项指控的认定，以及基于对所有四项指控均有罪的认定而录入的除名判决。本案发回工部局重新审议，以便根据前三项指控的认定结果，对惩罚判决进行相称且正当的调整和修改。诉讼费和律师费将由工部局承担。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
NOV 7 - 1939
Final Evidence
In Kelly Case
Court Commissioner Hears
Last Defence Witness in
Action Against S.M.C.

Insp. W. H. Widdowson, Personal
Assistant to the Deputy Commissioner
in Charge of Divisions, was a witness
yesterday afternoon when final evid-
ence was taken in the Court of
Consuls in the suit of former Det.
Sergt. Patrick J. Kelly against the
Shanghai Municipal Council. Mr.
Kelly, who was dismissed from the
force, contends that he was wrong-
fully discharged and that the S.M.C.
should pay him about £500 as due
him under the Police superannuation
scheme, $3,546 representing six
months' pay, money for the journey
of his wife and two children to Eng-
land, court fees, and $500.
The case is being heard by a Court
composed of Mr. Clarence E. Gauss,
American Consul-General, presiding;
Sir Herbert Phillips, H. M. Consul-
General, and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese
Consul-General. Mr. R. T. Bryan,
jun., Municipal Advocate, represented
the S.M.C., and Mr. H. A. Reeks the
petitioner. Mr. E. A. Long, sitting as
Commissioner of the Court, took
evidence yesterday.
Evidence given by Insp. Widdow-
son was mainly concerned with Mr.
Kelly's statement that he had been
coerced into making a certain peti-
tion to the Commissioner of Police.
Witness detailed the circumstances
which led to this petition being
submitted, covering conversations he
had with Mr. Kelly on May 4, 5
and 6 of this year, when Kelly saw
him about financial matters in con-
nection with the detective-sergeant's
dismissal from the force. Insp.
Widdowson said that he told peti-
tioner during those interviews that
he thought he (the petitioner) was
entitled only to his own contribu-
tions to the superannuation fund
but that the S.M.C. most likely
would be prepared to add to this
amount owing to Kelly's having a
family to support.

Petition to Commissioner
Insp. Widdowson said he advised
petitioner that the Commissioner of
Police was not inclined to change
his mind about the dismissal, but
that he might be ready to help the
ex-sergeant get a better financial
treatment on leaving. The making
of a petition to the Commissioner
was then discussed, and Kelly pre-
pared a letter which, however, did
not meet Insp. Widdowson's require-
ments for a petition, witness said,
as it did not actually plead.
Insp. Widdowson said he showed
Kelly's proposed letter to Capt.
H. M. Smyth, Deputy Commissioner,
and that Capt. Smyth agreed that
it was not the right kind of com-
munication in the circumstances.
With Insp. Widdowson's assistance,
Sergeant Kelly then prepared a
petition. The draft which Insp.
Widdowson gave the petitioner at
the time was shown in Court yester-
day and identified by the witness.

"Police Guide" Amendments
Mr. Bryan, the Municipal Advocate,
examined the witness at some length
about the Police Guide and Regula-
tions, prepared by witness for the use
of members of the force. Ins. Wid-
dowson explained that amendments
are made to this work from time to
time, but that the disciplinary rules
contained have not been amended in
recent years, nor have there been
changes in the rules governing the
making out of crime diaries by detec-
tives during the last several years.

起诉工部局案中的
最后一名辩方证人

负责各分区工作的副警务处长个人助理W. H. Widdowson巡官于昨日下午在领事法庭出庭作证，当时正在审理前警佐帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）起诉上海工部局一案的最后证据。凯利先生已被警队除名，他主张自己被非法解雇，并要求工部局支付约500英镑，这是根据警察退休金计划他应得的款项，包括代表六个月薪水的3,546美元、其妻子和两个孩子返回英国的旅费、法庭费用以及500美元。

本案由一个法庭审理，成员包括：主审的美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）先生、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯（Herbert Phillips）爵士，以及日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）先生。市政律师R. T. Bryan Jr. 先生代表工部局，H. A. Reeks 先生代表申请人。担任法院专员的E. A. Long 先生于昨日听取了证据。

Widdowson巡官提供的证词主要涉及凯利先生的说法，即他被胁迫向警务处长提交某份请愿书。证人详细说明了导致提交这份请愿书的情况，包括他在今年5月4日、5日和6日与凯利先生的谈话，当时凯利就其被警队除名相关的财务事宜会见了他。Widdowson巡官说，在这些面谈期间，他告诉申请人，他认为申请人（即申请人）仅有权获得其本人向退休基金缴纳的份额，但鉴于凯利有需要抚养的家庭，工部局很可能愿意在此金额基础上增加补助。

致处长的请愿书

Widdowson巡官说，他建议申请人，警务处长不太可能改变关于除名的决定，但他可能愿意帮助这位前警佐在离职时获得更好的财务待遇。随后讨论了向处长提交请愿书的事宜，凯利准备了一封信，但证人说，这封信不符合Widdowson巡官对请愿书的要求，因为它实际上并未提出诉求。

Widdowson巡官说，他将凯利拟议的信件出示给副警务处长H. M. Smyth上尉，Smyth上尉同意认为在当时情况下这不是合适的沟通方式。在Widdowson巡官的协助下，凯利警佐随后准备了一份请愿书。Widdowson巡官当时交给申请人的草稿于昨日在法庭上出示，并由证人辨认。

《警察指南》修订

市政律师Bryan先生就《警察指南》和《规章条例》对证人进行了 lengthy 的询问，该指南和条例由证人为警队成员使用而编制。Widdowson巡官解释说，这部作品会不时进行修订，但其中包含的纪律规则近年来并未修订，过去几年中关于侦探填写《犯罪日记》的规则也没有变化。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
NOV 4 - 1939

Further Evidence In Kelly
Case Heard Yesterday

Crime Diary Explained To Court Of Consuls By
Police Witness; Alleged Hiding Up Of
Visit To Taku Road; The Car Book

The charge that opposing counsel
was trying to "predicate" the
opinions of police officers called as
witnesses and was asking hypothe-
tical questions was made by Mr.
R. T. Bryan, Jnr., Municipal Advo-
cate, at the adjourned hearing yes-
terday afternoon in the Court of
Consuls of the $30,000 action for
alleged wrongful dismissal brought
by ex-Detective-Sergeant P. J.
Kelly against the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council.

The evidence of police officers
called as witnesses yesterday was
taken by Mr. E. A. Long, Secretary
of the Court, although at the pre-
vious hearings the case was heard
before Mr. Clarence E. Gauss,
American Consul-General (presid-
ing) Sir Herbert Phillips, British
Consul-General and Mr. Y. Miura,
Japanese Consul-General, Mr. H. A.
Reeks of Messrs. Ellis and Hays
appeared for Mr. Kelly, the
petitioner, while the case for the
Council was conducted by Mr.
Bryan.

Counsel To File Briefs

The hearing yesterday which
was featured by protestations and
objections by both counsel re-
garding the procedure of question-
ing by each other was adjourned
indefinitely, it being intimated that
only one more police witness will
be called. The court will not hear
arguments by counsel which will
be in the form of briefs filed with
the court.

The police officers called to the
witness-stand were enjoined by
Mr. Reeks in cross-examination to
testify "purely in t'e interests of
justice, oblivious to all else." At
one stage Mr. Bryan declared that
Mr. Reeks was making statements
instead of confining himself to the
asking of questions from witnesses.
At another stage Mr. Reeks pro-
tested that Mr. Bryan was cross-
examining his own witness. Mr.
Long pointed out to both counsel
that the proceedings should be
direct questioning.

Petitioner it was disclosed at a
previous hearing was dismissed
from the Force after being tried
by Mr. H. D. M. Robertson, Assist-
ant Police Commissioner, on charges
of failing to make an entry in a
police document; improperly re-
leasing a prisoner and extortion.

Supt Mason's Evidence

The first witness called was
Superintendent J. Mason, officer in
charge of "C" Division, comprising
Hongkew, West Hongkew, Paoshing
Road and Dixwell Road branches.
Examined by Mr. Bryan witness
said he was the divisional detective
officer in charge of "A" Division
comprising Central, Louza and
Chengtu Road stations. Witness
said he was familiar with police
procedures both from the stand-
point of the legal and police de-
partments of the Council.

(批：C4)

《字林西报》。
1939年11月4日

昨日审理凯利案之进一步证据

警方证人向领事法庭解释“犯罪日记”；被指隐瞒塘沽路之行；汽车登记簿

市政律师R. T. Bryan Jr.先生在昨天下午于领事法庭举行的续审中指出，对方律师试图“预设”作为证人出庭的警官的意见，并提出假设性问题。此次庭审涉及前警佐P. J. Kelly指控上海公共租界工部局不当解雇、索赔30,000美元的诉讼。

昨日出庭作证的警方警官之证词由法庭秘书E. A. Long先生记录，尽管在前几次听证中，案件是由美国总领事Clarence E. Gauss先生（主审）、英国总领事Sir Herbert Phillips和日本总领事Y. Miura先生审理的。Ellis and Hays律师事务所的H. A. Reeks先生代表申请人Kelly先生，而Bryan先生则代表工部局进行辩护。

律师将提交诉状摘要

昨天的听证会以双方律师就相互询问程序提出抗议和反对为特征，现已无限期休庭，据暗示将仅再传唤一名警方证人。法庭将不听取律师的口头辩论，而是以向法庭提交的诉状摘要形式进行。

Reeks先生在交叉盘问中告诫出庭作证的警官们“纯粹为了正义作证，不顾及其他一切”。在某一阶段，Bryan先生声称Reeks先生是在发表陈述，而非局限于向证人提问。在另一阶段，Reeks先生抗议Bryan先生正在交叉盘问己方证人。Long先生向双方律师指出，诉讼程序应为直接询问。

在前一次听证中披露，申请人在被副警务处长H. D. M. Robertson先生审判后遭警队开除，罪名包括未在警方文件中做记录、不当释放囚犯以及敲诈勒索。

梅森督察的证词

第一位被传唤的证人是J. Mason督察，他是负责包含虹口、西虹口、宝兴路和狄思威路分巡捕房的“C”区的负责人。在Bryan先生的讯问下，证人表示他曾担任负责包含中央捕房、老闸捕房和成都路捕房的“A”区的区刑事探员。证人表示，他从工部局法律和警务部门的角度熟悉警务程序。

that he had conducted inquiries
into the case against Mr. Kelly.
The complaining witness in the
case accompanied by a lawyer,
witness said, saw him on March

Asked to explain what prelimin-

Questioned next regarding a

Robertson, the Assistant Police

Personal diaries of officers,
witness continued, were important
as a safeguard to each officer

证人继续向法庭陈述，他已对针对Kelly先生的案件进行了调查。证人称，本案的控告证人在一名律师的陪同下，于去年3月31日会见了证人，因此证人从控告人处取得了一份供词。次日，他从控告人的妻子和兄弟处取得了其他供词，并安排进行某些调查，随后又取得了更多供词。证人表示，他奉Robertson先生之命启动初步调查，随后拟定了针对Kelly先生的指控。

当被要求根据警务规章解释“初步调查”的含义时，证人陈述道，当警官的行为受到质疑时便会进行调查。证人称，涉事警官无需出席调查，调查内容包括审查证据，以确定是否有理由对特定警官提出指控。

接下来，关于一份警方犯罪日记的问题被提出，该日记在之前的听证中被律师幽默地称为“著名的犯罪日记”，证人解释说这是一份官方警方文件，其主要目的是记录警官在调查过程中采取的所有行动，以供总部及其上级官员知晓；向他们通报调查进展以及与案件相关的处理情况。证人解释说，犯罪日记一是供警方使用，二是在实施逮捕和提起刑事诉讼时供市政律师使用。他说，涉案日记是警务处的财产，市政律师仅将其用于法律程序目的。在证人看来，该日记在刑事案件中非常重要。

“个人日记”

证人随后就被问及警官的“个人日记”或值班表，他解释说这使警官能够记录其行踪。证人称，高级警官会定期查阅此日记。

申请人在前一次听证中告诉法庭，警队成员并未严格执行某些警务规章制度。Bryan先生就此点向证人提问时，证人宣称据其所知，这些规定得到了遵守。

在告诉法庭他全程出席了Kelly先生的审判后，证人同意律师的说法，即申请人当时并未对由副警务处长Robertson先生审理此案提出任何异议。证人强调，Kelly被允许自由询问所有证人。

证人继续说道，警官的个人日记作为对每位警官的保障至关重要，

should there ever be any question
regarding his conduct.
Witness further told the court
that, as far as he saw, Mr. Robert-
son did not show any bias or
prejudice against Kelly during his
trial, but appeared to be fair and
impartial.
Cross-examined by Mr. Reeks
witness agreed that it was possible
for the diaries of other officers to
be kept in the way Kelly kept his
diary. Petitioner told the court at
a previous hearing that many
officers kept their diaries like him
and gave the names of several
officers when taxed by the Muni-
cipal Advocate to do so. Witness
went on to say that it would be
dangerous for an officer not to keep
his diary up to date for two
reasons: (1) he would not be
complying with police instructions
and (2) he was surrendering a
protection which might be afforded
him if required at a later date, to
clear himself if any question was
raised regarding his conduct.
Tahu Road Visit
Mr. Reeks then asked witness:
"The only serious offence of Kelly
under the first and third charges,
is that he attempted to hide his
visit to Taku Road. Have you
even to-day a detective officer who,
say, would visit the General
Hospital and whose conduct was
not highly suspicious, and if you
found that in his duty roster he
had not mentioned this visit, what
would you do from a disciplinary
point of view?" Witness replied
that he would see what the officer
would have to say, adding that the
man might have some explanation
to offer. If the man said he had
forgotten to make the entry witness
explained that he would ask the
man to exercise more care in the
future.
Counsel next suggested to witness
that Kelly if he wanted to
"hide" his visit to Taku Road, he
would not have recorded the visit
in the motor car book of the
station. Witness replied that he
could not say what Kelly would
or would not have done.
The next question was: "Are
the detectives who were on this
Taku Road visit, Kelly's subord-
inates in the sense that they were
not attached to him?" Witness
replied that the detectives were
not personally attached to Kelly,
but were with him only in connec-
tion with any particular case.
Counsel: "Are you prepared to
say Kelly lied when he said he
was not present when the Chinese
detectives were questioned separate-
ly at his trial?"—"No."
It was stated at the previous
hearing that the complaining wit-
ness regarding one of the charges
against Mr. Kelly went to see the
police accompanied by a Chinese
lawyer. Witness next was asked
what professional misconduct the
lawyer was guilty of and replied
that as far as he knew the lawyer
in question had trifled with the
truth. Witness was asked if he
agreed that the lawyer was told
he was a "liar," although not in
direct words. Witness replied that
this was insinuated, which caused
Mr. Reeks to remark: "Thank you,
Sir."
Mr. James Barry, Police super-
intendent was the next witness
called. Reverting to the incidents
relating to Mr. Kelly's dismissal
witness said Kelly was suspended
from duty by him on April 1, last.
Later, witness said, he handed
Kelly, a list of the charges against
him and certain Chinese detectives
concerned. Witness said Kelly had
no remark to make and went on
to tell the court that petitioner
saw him daily and usually asked
him for instructions or "news."

证人进一步告诉法庭，就他所见，Robertson先生在审判期间并未对Kelly表现出任何偏见或成见，而是显得公平且公正。

在Reeks先生的交叉盘问下，证人同意其他警官有可能像Kelly那样保存日记。申请人在前一次听证中告诉法庭，许多警官都像他一样保存日记，并在市政律师的要求下列出了几名警官的名字。证人接着说，警官不及时更新日记是危险的，原因有二：(1) 他将不符合警方指令；(2) 他放弃了日后若因其品行受到质疑而需要自证清白时可能提供的保护。

塘沽路之行

Reeks先生随后问证人：“根据第一项和第三项指控，Kelly唯一的严重罪行是他试图隐瞒其塘沽路之行。你手下是否甚至有这样一名刑事探员，比如说，他去往总医院，其行为并不十分可疑，如果你发现他在值班表中未提及此次访问，从纪律角度你会怎么做？”证人回答说，他会听听该警官有何说法，并补充说此人可能会有一些解释。证人解释说，如果此人说是忘记做记录，他会要求此人今后更加小心。

律师随后向证人暗示，如果Kelly想要“隐瞒”其塘沽路之行，他就不会将该次访问记录在捕房的汽车登记簿中。证人回答说，他无法断言Kelly会或不会做什么。

下一个问题是：“参与此次塘沽路之行的刑事探员，在未隶属于Kelly的意义上，是他的下属吗？”证人回答说，这些刑事探员并非个人隶属于Kelly，而只是因特定案件与他在一起。

律师问：“你准备说Kelly在审判中表示当中国刑事探员被单独讯问时他不在场，这是在撒谎吗？”——“不。”

在前一次听证中曾陈述，关于针对Kelly先生的一项指控的控告证人，在一名中国律师的陪同下去见了警方。证人随后被问及该律师犯了何种职业不当行为，并回答说，据他所知，涉案律师对事实不够严肃（trifled with the truth）。证人被问及是否同意该律师被告知是个“骗子”，尽管没有直接使用这个词。证人回答说这是一种暗示，这导致Reeks先生评论道：“谢谢你，先生。”

下一位被传唤的证人是警务督察James Barry先生。回到与Kelly先生被解雇有关的事件，证人表示他于去年4月1日暂停了Kelly的职务。证人稍后说，他交给Kelly一份针对他的指控清单以及涉案的几名中国刑事探员的名单。证人称Kelly对此未作任何评论，并继续告诉法庭，申请人每天都见他，通常向他请示或打听“消息”。

证人随后告诉法庭，申请人有一次问他，Robertson先生是否有权审判他。证人说他告诉申请人，就警务规章而言，Robertson先生拥有此权限。

“我们在这里纯粹是为了正义。我们必须完全忘却其他一切。难道你没有告诉Kelly他有权要求由委员会审判吗？”（意指由委员会审判）。证人说他从未告诉Kelly此类事情，并强调他对警务规章非常熟悉，不会建议Kelly做错事。

轻微指控

证人承认，据他所知，针对Kelly的指控是轻微的。证人同意律师的说法，即Kelly若要向警务处长上诉，必须通过上级警官转呈。

随后，刑事探长W. Duncan提供了佐证，他说去年三月他是中央捕房的高级刑事探员，也是申请人的直接上级。当被问及Kelly访问塘沽路的那天时，证人认为申请人并非忙得无法在个人日记中记录此次访问。证人还表示他出席了申请人的审判，并认为Robertson先生相当公平。他还告诉法庭，申请人获得了交叉盘问证人的充分机会。证人同意律师的说法，即塘沽路调查是一起小案。他也同意Reeks先生的说法，即在英国法律中，没有比敲诈勒索更严重的“黑色犯罪”（Black Crime，原文如此，疑为Blacker之误或特定表述）。他知道涉及塘沽路事件的中国警官失去了在工部局的养老金基金，金额分别为400美元和500美元。他同意他们随后未在中国法院被起诉，但解释说这不是由他决定的事项。

“他们为了逃避本应承受的起诉和惩罚而牵连Kelly？”Reeks先生随即向证人发难，证人回答：“我说不上来。”

当被问及：“你不认为关于Kelly被牵……”

being prosecuted?".
Counsel: "Are you hostile to
Kelly?"—"No, Sir."
"You indignantly deny that?"—
"Certainly".
"Have you ever made any effort
to find out whether in his personal
diary Kelly failed to enter places
which he visited?" Witness replied
that he had not.
Other Diaries
Sub-Inspector E. Davies then en-
tered the witness-box and identi-
fied two detective diaries as his
own. He said Kelly was at one time
stationed with him at the Bubbling
Well Station. Witness said petitioner
had never asked to see his diary
which was always on his desk. Cross-
examined witness declared that he
always entered in his diary the
places he visited. He agreed with
counsel that occasionally by acci-
dent an officer may fail to make
such an entry.
The last witness called was De-
tective Sub-Inspector Robert Fran-
cis who identified a diary as his
personal diary. He said he knew
petitioner and worked with him at
the Central station. He told the
court that Kelly had never asked
to see his diary and added that it
was not to his knowledge, whether
petitioner had ever done so. Cross-
examined witness said Kelly had no
business to look at his diary. To
the best of his knowledge, witness
said, his diary contained all the
places he visited. He agreed with
counsel that a mistake may arise
and an entry omitted through rush
of work.

律师：“你对凯利（Kelly）怀有敌意吗？”——“不，先生。”
“你愤然否认这一点吗？”——
“当然”。
“你是否曾努力查证凯利在其个人日记中是否漏记了他所访问的地点？”证人回答说他未曾这样做。

其他日记
副督察 E. 戴维斯（E. Davies）随后进入证人席，并指认两本侦探日记为其本人所有。他说凯利曾一度与他一同驻守于静安寺捕房（Bubbling Well Station）。证人称，申诉人从未要求查看他的日记，而该日记一直放在他的办公桌上。在交叉询问中，证人声明他总是在日记中记录他所访问的地点。他同意律师的说法，即警官偶尔可能因疏忽而未作此类记录。
最后传召的证人是侦探副督察罗伯特·弗朗西斯（Robert Francis），他指认一本日记为其个人日记。他说他认识申诉人，并曾在中央捕房与其共事。他告诉法庭，凯利从未要求查看他的日记，并补充说，据他所知，申诉人是否曾这样做他并不知情。在交叉询问中，证人称凯利无权查看他的日记。据他所知，证人表示，他的日记包含了他所访问的所有地点。他同意律师的说法，即可能会发生错误，或因工作繁忙而漏记条目。

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 4 - 1938
Officers' Crime
Diaries Given
As Evidence
Superintendent Mason
Appears For Council
At Hearing
DIARY ENTRIES
SAID REQUIRED
'Wrongful Dismissal' By
Police Complained
By P.J. Kelly
Evidence produced by the defense
in the suit of Patrick John Kelly,
former S.M.P. sergeant against the
Shanghai Municipal Council, ap-
parently to establish the alleged
misconduct of the plaintiff, was
featured at yesterday's hearing at
the Court of Consuls.
With Mr. E. A. Long, Secretary
to the Consular Body presiding as
Special Commissioner, the court
heard the evidence given
by Superintendent J. Mason, In-
spector W. Duncan, Sub-Inspector
E Davies and Sergeant Robert
Francis, British members of the
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Complaining against alleged
wrongful dismissal, Mr. Kelly
in the suit demanded that
the Council pay him £500 from the
superannuation fund, $3,546 re-
presenting six months' salaries and
$340 for court costs. An additional
sum, sufficient for a second class
passage home for himself and his
family, was also asked.
Diary Kept
Yesterday's witnesses, called by
the defense, were former superiors
and colleagues of the plaintiff. As
revealed by Superintendent Mason,
each of them stated that in com-
pliance with police regulations, he
kept a crime diary showing his
movement each day whether on
duty or off duty.
Apparently in an effort to prove
that the failure to make entries into
a diary is not wrongful, attorney
for the plaintiff asked Inspector
Kelly what he would do to an
officer if such entries had not been
duly made.
If nothing suspicious had come
to his knowledge, the inspector re-
plied, he would disregard the
failure.
Inspector Testifies
Following Inspector Duncan on
the stand, each of the other of-
ficers told the court that he kept
a crime diary as required. While it
was customary for them regularly
to make entries into the diaries, it
was added, it was possible that
mistakes might occur.
Five sets of the witnesses' diaries
were submitted in evidence by the
counsel for the defense, Mr. R. T.
Bryan, Jr., Municipal Advocate and
head of the S.M.C. Legal Depart-
ment, presented the case for the
police.
Mr. H. A. Reeks, member of the
law firm of Messrs. Ellis and Hays,
is attorney for the plaintiff.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。
1938年11月4日
警官犯罪
日记作为
证据提交
梅森总监
代表工部局
出席听证会
称日记条目
为必需事项
前警员投诉
遭“不当解雇”
在昨日领事法院的听证会上，前上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）巡长帕特里克·约翰·凯利（Patrick John Kelly）起诉上海公共租界工部局一案中，辩方提供的证据成为焦点，这些证据显然是为了确立原告所谓的不当行为。
由领事团秘书 E. A. 朗（E. A. Long）先生担任特别专员主持，法庭听取了上海公共租界工部局警务处英籍成员、总监 J. 梅森（J. Mason）、督察 W. 邓肯（W. Duncan）、副督察 E. 戴维斯（E. Davies）和巡长罗伯特·弗朗西斯（Robert Francis）提供的证词。
凯利先生投诉称其遭到不当解雇，在该诉讼中要求工部局从养老金基金中支付给他500英镑，3,546美元（相当于六个月薪水），以及340美元的诉讼费用。他还要求追加一笔足以供其本人及家人乘坐二等舱回国的费用。

保留日记
昨日由辩方传召的证人是原告的前上司和同事。正如梅森总监所透露，他们均陈述，根据警务规定，每个人都保留了一本犯罪日记，记录其每日的行踪，无论是否在执勤。
为了证明未在日记中作记录并非不当行为，原告的律师显然试图通过询问凯利督察，如果此类条目未按规定填写，他会如何处置涉事警官。
督察回答说，如果他没有得知任何可疑情况，他将忽略这种遗漏。

督察作证
继邓肯督察出庭后，其他每位警官都告诉法庭，他们按规定保留了犯罪日记。虽然定期在日记中作记录是他们的惯例，但有人补充说，错误仍有可能发生。
辩方律师、工部局法律顾问兼工部局法律部主任 R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan, Jr.）先生提交了五套证人日记作为证据，并为警方陈述案情。
原告律师为埃利斯和海斯律师事务所（Messrs. Ellis and Hays）的 H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
26472
NOV 4 - 1939

Possession of Opium Said
More Serious Than Stealing

Further Witnesses Questioned in Court of Consuls
Case; Mr. Kelly to Testify at Next Hearing

FOUR witnesses gave evidence yesterday afternoon before Mr.
A. E. Long, acting as Commissioner of the Court of Consuls,
in the case in which Mr. Patrick J. Kelly, former detective-ser-
geant of the Shanghai Municipal Police, represented by Mr. H. A.
Reeks, is the petitioner and the Shanghai Municipal Council is the
defendant. Mr. Kelly claims that he has been wrongfully dismissed
from the S.M.P. and that the Council, represented by Mr. R. T.
Bryan jun., should pay to him a sum of about £500 which he
claims is due him under the superannuation scheme, $3,546 repre-
senting six months' salary, the money for the passages to England
for petitioner's wife and two children, court fees and $500.

Mr. Bryan, at the opening of yes-
terday's hearing, called Mr. J. Mason,
Superintendent of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, to the witness-box.
Mr. Mason told the court that he
was in charge of "C" Division and
that, at the request of Assistant
Commissioner H. D. M. Robertson, he
made preliminary inquiries into a
complaint of alleged extortion which
had been received against Mr. Kelly.
Witness stated that when he had com-
pleted his report, he passed it on to
Mr. Robertson who was in charge of
the trial.
Witness, in reply to a question, said
that it was not necessary that a per-
son charged with an offence should
be present at a preliminary inquiry.
In referring to the Crime Diary,
witness said that this book was pri-
marily for the use of the police force
rather than of the Municipal Advo-
cate. He said that these books were
the property of the police and not of
the legal department of the S.M.C.
In referring to personal diaries, wit-
ness said that these were used by
detectives so as to enable them to
record their movements. Rules and
regulations, witness continued, were
strictly followed within the police
force as far as he knew.

Petitioner Did Not Object
Asked whether Mr. Kelly had ever
objected to Mr. Robertson hearing the
case, witness replied in the negative.
He also stated that Mr. Kelly had
never objected to charges 4 and 5
being joined.
Mr. Kelly, witness continued, was
present throughout the trial. Asked
what procedure was followed when
an arrest was made by a constable,
witness stated that the arrest must
be recorded and that an F.I.R. (first
information report) must also be
made out.
Motorcar diaries, witness stated,
were not sent to headquarters but
to the officer in charge of each sta-
tion.
In referring to personal diaries
once more, witness said that their
primary function was to safeguard the
detective and that, as a rule, these
diaries did not go further than to
the senior detective in the station.
Asked for the reason for his pre-
sence at the trial, witness said that
he was there to safeguard the inter-
ests of Mr. Kelly and to assist him
if necessary. In reply to a further
question, witness stated that in his
opinion, Mr. Robertson was fair and
unbiased towards Mr. Kelly during
the trial.

《北华捷报》（NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS）。
26472
1939年11月4日

称持有鸦片
比盗窃更为严重

领事法院案件进一步讯问证人；凯利先生将在下次听证会上作证

昨日下午，四名证人在代理领事法院专员的 A. E. 朗（A. E. Long）先生面前作证。该案中，前上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探巡长帕特里克·J. 凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）先生（由 H. A. 里克斯先生代理）为申诉人，上海公共租界工部局为被告。凯利先生声称其被工部局警务处不当解雇，并要求由 R. T. 布莱恩 junior 先生代表的工部局向他支付约500英镑，他声称这是根据养老金计划应得之款项；3,546美元，相当于六个月薪水；用于申诉人妻子和两个孩子返回英国的船票费用；诉讼费以及500美元。

布莱恩先生在昨日听证会开始时，传召上海公共租界工部局警务处总监 J. 梅森（J. Mason）先生出庭作证。梅森先生告诉法庭，他负责“C”区，并应助理总监 H. D. M. 罗伯逊（H. D. M. Robertson）的要求，对针对凯利先生的所谓勒索投诉进行了初步调查。证人陈述，当他完成报告后，将其移交给负责审理此案的罗伯逊先生。
证人回答提问时说，被指控犯罪的人不必出席初步调查。
在提及犯罪日记时，证人表示，这本簿册主要是供警务处使用，而非供工部局法律顾问使用。他说这些簿册是警务处的财产，而非工部局法律部的财产。在提及个人日记时，证人表示，侦探使用这些日记是为了记录他们的行踪。证人继续说，就他所知，警务处内严格遵守各项规章条例。

申诉人未提出异议
当被问及凯利先生是否曾反对由罗伯逊先生审理此案时，证人予以否认。他还陈述，凯利先生从未反对将第4项和第5项指控合并审理。
证人继续说，凯利先生全程出席了审判。当被问及巡警执行逮捕时遵循何种程序时，证人陈述，必须记录逮捕行动，并且还必须制作一份初报（F.I.R.，即首次信息报告）。
证人陈述，汽车日记不送往总部，而是送往各捕房的负责人。
再次提及个人日记时，证人表示，其主要功能是保护侦探，且通常这些日记不会超出捕房高级侦探的查阅范围。
当被问及他出席审判的原因时，证人表示，他是为了维护凯利先生的利益并在必要时协助他。在回答进一步提问时，证人表示，在他看来，罗伯逊先生在审判期间对凯利先生公正且无偏见。

page_data.en:
Lawyer's Conduct Questioned
Cross-examined by Mr. Reeks, witness in reply to counsel's query as to why Mr. Robertson had considered the conduct of Mr. Tong, a lawyer, unprofessional, said that Mr. Tong had not been telling the truth and that Mr. Robertson had taken him with this.
He also agreed to Mr. Reek's contention that the personal diary of a detective is only seen by comparatively less important senior officers. He denied that he had seen the motorcar diary immediately the complaint was laid against Mr. Kelly, but agreed that this would have been possible. He also said that if Mr. Kelly had wanted to conceal his trip to the Takoo Road address, he would not have had to enter the trip on the motorcar diary.
In referring to the crime diary once again, witness agreed that it could be written in sections and that it may cover any number of days. If the final crime diary contained things done initially but which until then had been omitted, no inference against the detective would be made.
Witness also agreed to the fact that the crimes of which the Chinese respondents had been found guilty were very serious. In referring to the punishment meted out to these Chinese detectives, Mr. Mason stated that they had been dismissed from the force and that their losses were from between $300 to $500 each.
In answering Mr. Reeks further, witness said that eight other foreign detectives were on duty with him on March 31, and he refused to deny the possibility that of the 12 to 15 cases handled by the detectives on that day, eight might have had to pass through Mr. Kelly.

List of Cases Promised
At the request of Mr. Reeks and with the consent of Mr. Long, witness agreed that, without coming to the witness-box again, he would place before the court at its next hearing, a list of detectives on duty on that day, together with a list of cases handled by them so as to enable the court to see what proportion of the cases passed through Mr. Kelly.
Superintendent J. Barry, who, at the time was the officer in charge of Central Station, was next called to the witness-box and said that Mr. Kelly had come to see him after he (witness) had spoken to Inspector W. Duncan, Senior Detective of Central Station. He told Mr. Kelly about the hearing and Mr. Kelly replied that Mr. Duncan had already told him about it.
In reply to one of Mr. Kelly's queries, witness at the time told him that as far as he knew, Mr. Robertson could hear the case.
In reply to a question by counsel for the petitioner, witness stated that the letter which Mr. Kelly sent to the commissioner of police at the time, was a private letter and that had it been considered official, it would have been returned to him with the request that it be forwarded in accordance with regulations, namely through his directly superior officer.
page_data.zh:
律师行为受质疑
在里克斯先生的交叉询问下，证人回答律师关于为何罗伯逊先生认为童（Tong，音译）律师的行为不专业的问题时，表示童先生没有说实话，而罗伯逊先生对此心知肚明。
他还同意里克斯先生的观点，即侦探的个人日记仅由级别相对较低的高级警官查阅。他否认在针对凯利先生的投诉提出后立即查看了汽车日记，但承认这种情况是可能的。他还表示，如果凯利先生想要隐瞒他去塔古路（Takoo Road，音译）地址的行程，他无需在汽车日记中记录该次行程。
再次提及犯罪日记时，证人同意日记可以分段书写，并且可以涵盖任意天数。如果最终的犯罪日记包含了起初做过但直到那时才被补记的事项，则不会对侦探作出不利推断。
证人还同意这一事实，即被判有罪的中国涉案人员所犯罪行非常严重。在提及对这些中国侦探施加的惩罚时，梅森先生表示，他们已被开除出警务处，每人损失在300至500美元之间。
在进一步回答里克斯先生的提问时，证人表示，3月31日当天有另外八名外籍侦探与他一起执勤，他拒绝否认这样一种可能性：即在当天侦探处理的12至15起案件中，有八起可能经手过凯利先生。

承诺提供案件清单
应里克斯先生的请求并经朗先生同意，证人同意不再次出庭，而是在下次听证会上向法庭提交一份当日执勤侦探名单，以及他们所处理案件的清单，以便法庭了解有多少比例的案件经手过凯利先生。
接下来传召出庭作证的是 J. 巴里（J. Barry）总监，他当时是中央捕房的负责人。他说，在他（证人）与中央捕房高级侦探 W. 邓肯（W. Duncan）督察谈话后，凯利先生曾来见他。他告诉凯利先生有关听证会的事，凯利先生回答说邓肯先生已经告诉过他了。
回答凯利先生的一个询问时，证人当时告诉他，就他所知，罗伯逊先生可以审理此案。
回答申诉人律师的提问时，证人表示，凯利先生当时写给警务处处长的信是一封私人信件，如果被视为公函，它会被退回给他，并要求他按照规定，即通过其直接上级官员转交。

page_data.en:
Role of Crime Diaries
Inspector W. Duncan was next called to the witness-box. He said that all crime diaries at Central Station were forwarded to him and that the work done by Mr. Kelly on March 31, was not unusual as he only handled one important case, involving the snatching of $1,000. He further said that detectives on duty would work on whatever case came their way and
that on March 31, Mr. Kelly had enough time in which to fill out his crime diary. Mr. Mason, in the opinion of witness, was present at the trial in order to assist Mr. Kelly, witness was not prepared to say whether Mr. Kelly was entitled to have someone to help him at the trial in the capacity of a next friend. Witness also produced the personal diary of Mr. Dailey, a former detective of the S.M.P.
Witness would not agree with the suggestion of counsel for the petitioner, that a larceny of $5 was as serious as a larceny of $1,000 because, witness said, such a crime was looked upon differently. He also declined to agree that the possession of two ounces of opium in Shanghai was a less serious crime than the larceny of $5 because the District Court would inflict a much heavier punishment on an opium offence.
Mr. Duncan admitted—as Mr. Mason had done when he was in the witness-box—that during the questioning of the Chinese detectives who were respondents to charge 5, each respondent was questioned separately while the others were outside the room. Both witnesses also denied that Mr. Kelly had been absent during the individual questioning of the Chinese respondents.
Mr. Reeks then asked the court that at the next hearing he be permitted to ask petitioner to step into the witness-box and to state on oath that he was not present when the Chinese detectives were individually questioned.

Personal Diaries Produced
The next witness to be called to the box was Det. Sub-Inspector B. Davies who produced his personal diary and said that it had been lying on a desk in the same detective office in which Kelly was and that he had never asked Kelly to look at it. Det-Sergt. R. Francis made a similar statement from the witness-box.
In reply to a question by Mr. Reeks, both witnesses did not deny that if crime diaries were checked, it could be shown that they had frequently failed to mention in their personal diaries visits made to particular places.
Before the hearing was adjourned, Mr. Bryan told the court that he would call one more witness at the next hearing and it seemed likely that the case would then be concluded and that both counsel would submit their written arguments to the court presided over by Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, U. S. Consul-General, assisted by Sir Herbert Phillips, H. M. Consul-General, and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General.
Mr. Kelly, as will be recalled, was dismissed from the police force on having been found guilty of extortion.
page_data.zh:
犯罪日记的作用

随后，W. 邓肯（W. Duncan）督察被传唤至证人席。他表示，中央捕房的所有犯罪日记均转交给他处理，而凯利（Kelly）先生于3月31日所做的工作并无异常，因为他当时仅处理了一起涉及抢夺1,000美元的重要案件。他进一步指出，当值侦探会处理任何落到他们手中的案件，且在3月31日，凯利先生有足够的时间填写其犯罪日记。在证人看来，梅森（Mason）先生出席审判是为了协助凯利先生，但证人不愿就凯利先生是否有权在审判中由他人以“诉讼监护人”（next friend）的身份提供协助一事发表意见。证人还出示了前公共租界工部局警务处侦探戴利（Dailey）先生的个人日记。

证人不同意原告律师提出的暗示，即盗窃5美元与盗窃1,000美元同样严重，因为证人表示，此类犯罪受到的看待方式不同。他也不同意在上海持有两盎司鸦片比盗窃5美元的罪行较轻的说法，因为地方法院对鸦片犯罪施加的惩罚要严厉得多。

邓肯先生承认——正如梅森先生在证人席上所做的那样——在讯问作为第5项指控答辩人的中国侦探时，每位答辩人都是单独接受讯问的，而其他人在房间外等候。两位证人均否认凯利先生在中国籍答辩人接受单独讯问期间缺席。

随后，里克斯（Reeks）先生请求法庭允许他在下次听证时要求原告步入证人席，并宣誓声明在中国侦探接受单独讯问时他不在场。

出示个人日记

下一位被传唤至证人席的是侦探副督察 B. 戴维斯（B. Davies），他出示了自己的个人日记，并称该日记一直放在与凯利所在的同一间侦探办公室的桌子上，且他从未要求凯利查看过该日记。侦探警长 R. 弗朗西斯（R. Francis）在证人席上作了类似的陈述。

在回答里克斯先生的提问时，两位证人均未否认，如果核对犯罪日记，可以显示他们经常在个人日记中遗漏提及对特定地点的走访。

在听证会休庭前，布莱恩（Bryan）先生告知法庭，他将在下次听证时再传唤一名证人，案件似乎届时将告终结，且双方律师将向由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E. 高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）主持、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）先生协助组成的法庭提交书面辩论意见。

如前所述，凯利先生因被裁定犯有勒索罪而被开除出警察队伍。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
NOV 2 1939
264^1

Hearing On Kelly's Damage
Suit Against S.M.C. Continued

Police Commissioner Reiterates In Consular
Court That Plaintiff Had Fair Trial
Before Dismissal From Force

Under a gruelling two-hour cross-
examination before the Court of
Consuls yesterday, Assistant Com-
missioner of the S.M.P. Henry
Robertson, appearing as witness in
the Kelly lawsuit case, stood ada-
mant on the contention that his
former subordinate Detective Inspec-
tor P. J. Kelly had been given a
perfectly fair trial before being dis-
missed from the Shanghai force last
spring.
The case in which Kelly is suing
the Shanghai Municipal Council for
recovery of $30,000 which he claims
as his due for various sums of which
he was deprived when discharged,
was heard before Mr. Clarence E.
Gauss, American Consul-General,
Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-
General and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese
Consul-General, sitting as a court.
The hearings yesterday were
marked by sharp differences of
opinion as to procedure between the
two pleading attorneys, Mr. H. A.
Reeks, British lawyer who represent-
ed Kelly and Mr. R. T. Bryan Jr.,
American lawyer who as Municipal
Advocate represented the S.M.C.
At the opening of the hearing, Mr.
Bryan offered Mr. Kelly the super-
annuation of $2,444.10 on behalf of
the S.M.C. which the plaintiff had
once previously been tendered but
had refused.
Reeks Accepts
Speaking for his client, Mr. Reeks
agreed to accept the sum if accept-
ance would not prejudice Kelly's
case. The court assented to stipulation.
Commissioner Robertson, answer-
ing to the examination of Mr.
Bryan, said he had summoned Kelly
on March 31 to tell him that cer-
tain allegations had been made
against him and would require a
preliminary inquiry of which he
would be duly informed.
As a result of the investigations
carried out by Police Superintend-
ent Mason, a preliminary inquiry
was held and the trial itself started
April 13. Commissioner Robertson
said that Kelly must have known
he was appearing on trial and was
not attending a preliminary inquiry.
Of the four charges which had been
alleged against Kelly, only one was
brought against him in the trial,
that of failing to return a pistol,
ammunition and opium seized dur-
ing an arrest. Commissioner Robert-
son said he had told Kelly this
charge would be lodged and Kelly
had made no objection.
The remaining charges were: 1)
knowingly making a false statement
in the police crime diary, 2) un-
necessary detention of a Chinese
and then improperly releasing him;
3) wilfully making a false statement
in his own detective diary.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）
1939年11月2日
264^1

关于凯利损害
赔偿案的听证会继续进行
针对上海公共租界工部局的诉讼

警务处长在领事法庭重申
原告在被开除前获得了公正审判

昨日，在上海公共租界工部局警务处助理处长亨利·罗伯逊（Henry Robertson）作为证人出席凯利诉讼案，并在领事法庭接受长达两小时的严苛交叉盘问期间，他坚持认为，其前下属、侦探督察 P. J. 凯利（P. J. Kelly）在去年春季被开除出上海警察队伍之前，已获得完全公正的审判。

凯利起诉上海公共租界工部局，要求追回30,000美元，他声称这是他被解职时被剥夺的各项款项中应得的部分。该案由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E. 高斯先生、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士和日本总领事三浦先生组成合议庭进行审理。

昨日的听证会以两位代理律师在程序问题上的尖锐意见分歧为标志，分别是代表凯利的英国律师 H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生，以及作为工部局法律代表的美国律师 R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan Jr.）先生。

听证会开始时，布莱恩先生代表工部局向凯利先生提供2,444.10美元的退休金，这笔款项此前曾向原告提出但被拒绝。

里克斯接受

里克斯先生代表其当事人表示，如果接受该笔款项不会损害凯利的案件，他同意接受。法庭同意了这一约定。

罗伯逊处长在回答布莱恩先生的询问时表示，他于3月31日传唤凯利，告知有人对他提出某些指控，因此需要进行初步调查，并将正式通知他。

经警务总监梅森开展调查后，举行了初步调查，正式审判于4月13日开始。罗伯逊处长表示，凯利一定知道自己是在受审，而非参加初步调查。在被指控针对凯利的四项罪名中，只有一项在审判中被正式起诉，即未能归还逮捕期间缴获的手枪、弹药和鸦片。罗伯逊处长表示，他曾告知凯利将提出此项指控，而凯利并未提出异议。

其余指控为：1) 在警方犯罪日记中故意作出虚假陈述；2) 不必要地拘留一名中国人并随后不当释放；3) 在其个人侦探日记中故意作出虚假陈述。

page_data.en:
264:5

Testimony Detailed
The testimony of Commissioner
Robertson then became more detail-
ed as he explained the use of the
Police Crime Diary and of the De-
tective Crime diary which he said
it was important to keep up for
self-protection of the individual
officer against false allegations.
Later when asked whether he
had been prejudiced against Kelly
during the trial, Commissioner
Robertson said he very much regret-
ted that Kelly should have thought
him prejudiced as he had made
every effort to be fair, even asking
Kelly's immediate superior, the
Divisional Detective officer, to sit in
at the proceedings.
Cross-examination of the witness
by Mr. Reeks opened on a definite-
ly hostile key when counsel charged
Commissioner Robertson with hav-
ing omitted certain proceedings of
the trial from the record. This
pointed question, asked several
times in various ways, was answered
unswervingly in the negative by the
Assistant Commissioner
Mr. Reeks then accused the wit-
ness of ignorance of the police re-
gulations and pointed out that the
Commissioner of Police had sug-
gested that a board be appointed
to hear Kelly's case but that the
Assistant Commissioner had declar-
ed his ability to handle the matter
alone. To this the witness said he
would have been President of the
investigating board anyway.
Kelly Case "Clear"
Commissioner Robertson then re-
futed the implication that he had
tried Kelly with a preconceived
notion of his guilt. He declared
that he had merely been satisfied
that there was a clear case in the
matter.
Mr. Reeks said in a heated tone
that the fact was that there had
been not a shred of evidence against
Kelly. The Court asked counsel to
desist with argument and to pro-
ceed with questioning.
Further questioning elicited the
information from witness that
Kelly's mere omission of a proper
diary record was sufficient for dis-
charge. The cross-examination then
went into more details of technical
points on which Kelly had been
found guilty and came to a con-
clusion when Mr. Reeks discovered
that the court was becoming rest-
less.
The hearing which started at 4:30
p.m. was adjourned at 6:30 p.m.,
the Court deciding that future evi-
dence would be heard before Mr.
F. A. Long, Secretary sitting as
Examiner and Commissioner. Mr.
Bryan will bring two more witnesses
to the next hearing.
page_data.zh:
264:5

证词详述

随后，罗伯逊处长的证词变得更加详细，他解释了警方犯罪日记和侦探犯罪日记的用途，并称保持这些记录对于保护个别警官免受虚假指控至关重要。

后来，当被问及在审判期间是否对凯利抱有偏见时，罗伯逊处长表示，他对凯利认为他有偏见深感遗憾，因为他已尽一切努力保持公正，甚至邀请凯利的直接上级——分区侦探官——列席旁听程序。

里克斯先生对证人的交叉盘问以明显敌对的基调开始，律师指控罗伯逊处长在记录中遗漏了审判的某些程序。这一尖锐的问题以各种方式多次提出，助理处长均坚定不移地予以否认。

随后，里克斯先生指责证人对警察规章无知，并指出警务处长曾建议任命一个委员会来审理凯利的案件，但助理处长却宣称自己有能力单独处理此事。对此，证人表示，无论如何他都将是调查委员会的主席。

凯利案“事实清楚”

罗伯逊处长随后驳斥了有关他带着凯利有罪的先入之见对其进行审判的暗示。他宣称，他只是确信此案事实清楚。

里克斯先生语气激动地表示，事实是针对凯利的证据连一丝一毫都没有。法庭要求律师停止辩论，继续提问。

进一步的提问从证人处获悉，凯利仅仅未适当记录日记便足以构成开除理由。随后的交叉盘问深入探讨了凯利被判有罪的技术细节，直到里克斯先生发现法庭变得不耐烦时才结束。

听证会于下午4:30开始，于下午6:30休庭，法庭决定后续证据将由担任审查员和专员的秘书 F. A. 朗（F. A. Long）先生听取。布莱恩先生将在下次听证时再传唤两名证人。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
1939
26437

Kelly's Contribution To
Superannuation Fund Is
Paid By S.M.C. In Court

Cheque For $2,444.10 Handed Over At Third
Adjourned Hearing Of Former Detective's
Suit; Court Adjourns Indefinitely

ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER ROBERTSON
SEVERELY CROSS-EXAMINED

Payment of a cheque for $2,444.10 to former Detective-
Sergeant Patrick J. Kelly, being his contribution to his super-
annuation fund, was made by the Shanghai Municipal Council
in the Court of Consuls yesterday afternoon, at the third
adjourned hearing of the trial of Mr. Kelly's case against the
Council. The cheque was accepted by Mr. Kelly's counsel, Mr.
H. A. Reeks, of Messrs. Ellis and Hays, without prejudice to
his client's entire claim, amounting to approximately $30,000,
for superannuation fund, six months' pay in lieu of notice and
second class passages to England for himself, his wife and
children.

Mr. R. T. Bryan, Jr., Municipal
Advocate for the Council, tendered
the cheque after it had been dis-
closed at the previous hearing that
the ex-police officer, who was dis-
missed from the Force, was entirely
bereft of means and was living on
dependencies of his former brother
officers, who, he said, had even
lent him money to defray the pas-
sage of his family back to Eng-
land.

Rift Between Counsel
Another rift was occasioned at
the trial of the case yesterday by
sharp exchanges between counsel,
Mr. Reeks at one stage accusing
Mr. Bryan of being lacking in
courtesy, which provoked the re-
tort that the accuser should keep
his temper.

The case was heard in Council
chambers before Mr. Clarence E.
Gauss, American Consul-General
(president); Sir Herbert Philipps,
British Consul-General and Mr.
Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General.
The only witness called was Mr.
Henry Robertson, Assistant Police
Commissioner, after which the
court adjourned indefinitely after
intimating that other witnesses
called by the Council would be
heard by a commissioner, probably
the secretary of the court. It was
also stated that arguments by
counsel would be in the nature of
briefs filed with the court.

Mr. Robertson was the first
witness for the Council and was
examined at some length by Mr.
Bryan and at greater length by
Mr. Reeks, who subjected him to
a severe barrage of questioning
during which counsel suggested to
witness that certain Chinese de-
tectives in the Force were keen
to get Mr. Kelly implicated, to
divert proceedings against them-
selves in the District Court.
Witness replied that he did not
know what was in the minds of
the detectives.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）
1939年
26437

上海公共租界工部局在法庭上
支付凯利对退休基金的供款

在前侦探诉讼案第三次延期听证的会上，移交了一张金额为2,444.10美元的支票；法庭无限期休庭

助理处长罗伯逊
遭受严厉交叉盘问

昨日下午，在凯利先生起诉工部局一案的第三次延期听证会上，上海公共租界工部局在领事法庭向前侦探警长帕特里克·J. 凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）支付了一张金额为2,444.10美元的支票，作为其对退休基金的供款。凯利的律师、来自埃利斯和海斯律师事务所（Messrs. Ellis and Hays）的 H. A. 里克斯先生接受了该支票，但这并不损害其当事人总额约30,000美元的全部索赔权利，其中包括退休基金、代替通知期的六个月薪水，以及为其本人、妻子和子女返回英国的二等舱船票。

工部局法律顾问 R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan Jr.）先生在得知前警官（已被开除出警队）身无分文、靠昔日同僚接济生活后，递交了该支票。据称，这些同僚甚至借钱给他支付家人返回英国的路费。

律师间的裂痕

昨日的案件审理中，律师之间的激烈交锋再次引发裂痕，里克斯先生在某一阶段指责布莱恩先生缺乏礼貌，这招致反驳，称指控者应保持冷静。

该案在美国总领事克拉伦斯·E. 高斯先生（主席）、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士和日本总领事三浦先生面前，于工部局会议室进行了审理。唯一被传唤的证人是助理警务处长亨利·罗伯逊先生，此后法庭宣布无限期休庭，并暗示工部局传唤的其他证人将由一名专员（可能是法庭秘书）听取证词。另据悉，律师的辩论将以向法院提交的简报形式进行。

罗伯逊先生是工部局的第一位证人，他先接受了布莱恩先生较长时间的询问，随后又接受了里克斯先生更长时间的询问。里克斯先生对其进行了严厉的连环质问，期间律师向证人暗示，警队中的某些中国侦探急于牵连凯利先生，以转移地方法院针对他们自身的诉讼程序。证人回答说，他不知道这些侦探心里在想什么。

page_data.en:
264

Severe Cross-Examination
During the cross-examination, Mr. Bryan on several occasions objected to the line of questioning adopted by Mr. Reeks, and at one stage declared that witness could not be expected to answer arguments. Mr. Bryan suggested that Mr. Reeks was arguing the case instead of cross-examining witness. The latter, during cross-examination, told Mr. Reeks that he (counsel) did not understand the procedure of the Police Force.
At another stage Mr. Reeks suggested to the Assistant Police Commissioner that he himself had made statements showing that he also did not know police regulations. Counsel also suggested that witness was "growing careless" in trying cases against police officers after witness had emphasized that he had tried many cases, at regular intervals of once every three months.
Witness, it was disclosed, had tried Mr. Kelly, who was charged on four laid charges of not making an entry in an official record etc. Mr. Kelly admitted the charge previously but declared that his offence was technical, not wilful or intentional. The counsel submitted that for a trivial offence he was visited with the maximum of punishment, namely dismissal from the Force and forfeiture of his superannuation fund.
Arrest—With Qualifications
At the close of the proceedings yesterday Mr. L... tendered a cheque to Mr. Kelly. Before it acceptance Mr. Reeks pointed out that it was unusual in the course of civil proceedings, when an action is brought for sums of money, to tender anything in payment. The money in the opinion of counsel should have been paid into court. In accepting the cheque Mr. Reeks emphasized that he was doing so on the understanding that the court would not infer that this was the total sum claimed.
Mr. Robertson, during a long examination, told the court that he was in charge of "A" Division of the Force and responsible for the officers in that division and had full control of all members of the police force in that department. After stating that petitioner had appeared before him in March, witness continued: "I told Sergeant Kelly that certain allegations had been made against him and that these inquiries would be made the subject of preliminary investigations by the detective divisional officer, Superintendent Mason. I told Kelly he would be notified of the results of these investigations in due course."
Asked what preliminary inquiry meant, witness said it was laid down in police regulations that when allegations are made against an officer, the divisional officer will conduct a preliminary inquiry himself or impute a subordinate to do so. A preliminary inquiry consists of detectives' investigations into the allegations made.
page_data.zh:
264

严厉盘问
在盘问过程中，布莱恩先生（Mr. Bryan）多次对里克斯先生（Mr. Reeks）采用的提问方式提出异议，并在某一阶段宣称，不能期望证人回答辩论性的问题。布莱恩先生指出，里克斯先生是在就案件进行辩论，而非对证人进行盘问。后者在盘问期间告诉里克斯先生，他（指律师）并不了解警队的程序。
在另一阶段，里克斯先生向助理警务处长暗示，该证人自己曾发表过表明其同样不了解警务规章的言论。辩护律师还暗示，证人在强调自己每三个月定期审理许多案件之后，却在审理针对警官的案件时变得“粗心大意”。
据披露，证人曾审理凯利先生（Mr. Kelly）一案，凯利被控四项罪名，包括未在官方记录中进行登记等。凯利此前承认了指控，但声称其过错属于技术性违规，并非故意或蓄意。辩护律师提出，对于这一轻微过错，凯利却受到了最严厉的惩罚，即被开除出警队并没收其养老金基金。

附条件逮捕
在昨日的诉讼程序结束时，L...先生向凯利先生递交了一张支票。在接受之前，里克斯先生指出，在涉及金钱索赔的民事诉讼过程中，直接提交款项作为支付是不寻常的。辩护律师认为，这笔钱本应存入法院。里克斯先生在接收支票时强调，他这样做是基于一种谅解，即法院不会推断这是所索赔的全部金额。
罗伯逊先生（Mr. Robertson）在长时间的讯问中告诉法庭，他负责警队“A”分区，对该分区的警官负责，并完全掌控该部门所有警员。在陈述请愿人曾于三月出现在他面前之后，证人继续说道：“我告诉凯利巡佐，有人对他提出了某些指控，这些调查将由侦探分区主管梅森警司（Superintendent Mason）进行初步调查。我告诉凯利，这些调查的结果将在适当时候通知他。”
当被问及初步调查的含义时，证人表示，警务规章规定，当对警官提出指控时，分区主管将亲自进行初步调查，或指派下属进行。初步调查包括侦探对所作指控进行的调查。

page_data.en:
26420

Need Not Be Present
Witness emphasized that, according to police regulations, it was not necessary for respondent officers to such inquiries, to be present at a preliminary inquiry into allegations made against him. The same he said applied in the case of Mr. Kelly. The latter laid strenuous objections at a previous hearing to the inquiry in his absence.
Mr. Robertson further told the court that the record taken at the inquiry was accurate, taken by witnesses in long-hand. To obviate the possibility of erroneous recording, witness said, he had a divisional officer sit beside him.
Witness went on to tell the court that he did not find Kelly guilty of "attempted extortion." Questioned regarding the detectives' crime diary, witness emphasized that every detective in the force received personal diaries in which they were supposed to record all their movements. This crime diary was, in the opinion of witness, one of the most important books in the force; when filled it must be kept for five years before being destroyed. Time and dates must be entered according to instructions in the book as well as places visited and nature of such visits. These for the information of the senior detective in a particular station, so that a check may be kept on the work of detectives, and for the information of headquarters as well as for the protection of the detectives themselves when allegations are made against them.
Questioned regarding the First Crime Diary, witness said this should be made out in all cases of crimes reported in a station, and the information imparted must be accurate. This information is forwarded to the deputy commissioner in charge of a crime branch. Although he may not see trivial cases, witness said, the diary would be sent to this official all the same.
In the case of an arrest a copy of the entry in the diary would be sent to the Municipal Advocate, to assist him to present a case to the court. The primary purpose of the diary, witness continued, was for the use of the police force It should contain accounts of investigations carried out by an officer in connection with each case. If no arrest followed, the account would be filed away after the completion of the investigation. Witness emphasized that detectives in the force were strictly required to carry this out. A foreign officer, witness said, would write his report in longhand, to be typed out later by a Chinese clerk.
Questioned regarding the function of foreign detectives witness said their duty was to keep Chinese detectives under control and prevent abuses by them and also to control investigations. The moment a foreign detective took up a case witness explained, he would be responsible for the subsequent investigations and the Chinese detectives concerned would act as his subordinates.

26420

无需在场
证人强调，根据警务规章，面对针对其提出的指控进行初步调查时，涉事警官无需在场。他说，这也适用于凯利先生的情况。后者在先前的听证会上强烈反对在他缺席的情况下进行调查。
罗伯逊先生进一步告诉法庭，调查期间所做的记录是准确的，由速记员以手写速记方式记录。为了避免错误记录的可能性，证人表示，他让一名分区主管坐在他旁边。
证人接着告诉法庭，他并未认定凯利犯有“企图勒索”罪。当被问及侦探的犯罪日记时，证人强调，警队中的每名侦探都配有个人日记，他们应在其中记录所有的行动轨迹。证人认为，这本犯罪日记是警队中最重要的簿册之一；写满后必须保存五年方可销毁。必须按照日记中的指示填写时间和日期，以及访问的地点和访问性质。这些信息供特定警署的高级侦探查阅，以便监督侦探的工作，同时也供总部查阅，并在侦探受到指控时保护他们自身。
当被问及第一犯罪日记（First Crime Diary）时，证人表示，警署报告的所有案件都应制作此日记，且所提供的信息必须准确。这些信息会转交给负责犯罪部门的副警务处长。证人说，虽然他可能不看琐碎的案件，但日记无论如何都会送给这位官员。
在逮捕案件中，日记条目的副本将发送给市公诉人（Municipal Advocate），以协助其向法庭提出案件。证人继续说，日记的主要目的是供警队使用。它应包含警官针对每个案件进行的调查记录。如果没有随后发生逮捕，调查完成后该记录将被归档。证人强调，警队中的侦探被严格要求执行此规定。证人表示，外籍警官会以手写方式撰写报告，随后由华籍职员打字录入。
当被问及外籍侦探的职能时，证人表示，他们的职责是管控华籍侦探，防止其滥用职权，并控制调查工作。证人解释说，一旦外籍侦探接手案件，他就对后续调查负责，相关的华籍侦探将作为他的下属行事。
