26440

Que...ed regarding the pro-
cedure for the release of a prisoner.
witness explained: "All persons
released must be release through
the charge room, through the
officer on charge room duty. An
arrest must also be reported to the
same official and it would be an
irregularity on the part of an
officer not to report a release.
Witness went on to say that an
officer should only draw his pistol
before entering a place where
armed resistance was expected
from the occupants. If a foreign
detective enters a place, he ex-
plained, with drawn pistol, he
should see to it that the Chinese
detectives accompanying him also
have drawn pistols.
Knew It Was "Trial"
Witness next was questioned re-
garding Kelly's trial and opined that
petitioner knew it was a "trial."
Questioned regarding a Chinese
lawyer who went to the detective
divisional office with the complain-
ant in the case, witness denied call-
ing the lawyer a "liar," as alleged
by Kelly at a previous hearing. As
a divisional officer, witness empha-
sized that he would not use such
language before his subordinates.
Witness said he accused the lawyer
of being guilty of unprofessional
conduct, which in his opinion should
be brought to the notice of the
bar association. Witness went on
to say that Kelly had every oppor-
tunity to question witnesses at his
trial. Regarding the second listed
charge against Kelly of releasing a
prisoner improperly, witness said
this was an irregularity as the man
had not been released through the
charge room. Questioned regard-
ing the torture of prisoners, wit-
ness declared that this was not
allowed under any circumstances
and explained that a foreign officer
was responsible for any torture by
his Chinese subordinates.
During the cross-examination Mr.
Reeks suggested to witness that the
police crime diary was not always
entered up the same day an in-
vestigation was held into a case.
Counsel said it would be a sur-
prise if he called evidence to show
that in one case a detective ser-
geant in Chengtu Road station was
told that he would get into trouble
because he had not written up the
diary for a fortnight.
After a protracted questioning in
which Mr. Reeks accused witness
of deliberately misleading the court,
counsel suggested that witness had
found his client guilty of the charge
not because he thought Kelly was
concerned in any blackmailing with
others, but because he had not made
an entry in a book in accordance
"With these strict rules and police
regulations." Witness replied that
he had found Kelly guilty on the
evidence before him.

当被问及释放囚犯的程序时，
证人解释道：“所有获释人员
必须通过收押室，经由值勤的
收押室警官办理释放。逮捕也
必须向同一位官员报告，如果
警官不报告释放情况，则属违
规行为。”
证人接着说，警官只应在进入
预计居住者会进行武装抵抗的
场所之前拔出手枪。他解释
道，如果外籍侦探持出鞘手枪
进入某处，他应确保陪同他的
华籍侦探也拔出手枪。
知道那是“审判”
证人随后被问及凯利的审判情
况，他认为请愿人知道那是一
次“审判”。当被问及一名随同
该案投诉人前往侦探分区办公
室的华籍律师时，证人否认曾
称该律师为“骗子”，正如凯利
在先前的听证会上所指控的那
样。作为一名分区主管，证人
强调，他不会在下属面前使用
此类语言。证人表示，他指责
该律师犯有不专业行为，他认
为这应提请律师公会注意。证
人接着说，凯利在审判中有充
分的机会质询证人。关于针对
凯利的第二项列名指控，即不
当释放囚犯，证人表示这是一
种违规行为，因为该人并未通
过收押室获释。当被问及拷打
囚犯的问题时，证人声明这在
任何情况下都是不允许的，并
解释说，外籍警官需对其华籍
下属的任何拷打行为负责。
在盘问过程中，里克斯先生向
证人暗示，警方的犯罪日记并
不总是在案件调查当天进行登
记。辩护律师称，如果他传唤
证据显示，在成都路（Chengtu Road）警署的一名侦探巡佐
被告知，因为他两周未填写日
记而将遇到麻烦，这会令人吃
惊。
经过长时间的讯问，里克斯先
生指责证人故意误导法庭，辩
护律师暗示，证人判定其当事
人有罪，并非因为他认为凯利
与他人参与任何勒索活动，而
是因为他未按照“这些严格的
规则和警务规章”在簿册中进
行登记。证人回答说，他是根
据呈堂证据判定凯利有罪的。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
264.7

Former Police Sergeant's
Case Against Council

Court of Consuls Hears Evidence of Divisional
Officers ; Case Again Adjourned

MR. H. D. M. Robertson, Assistant Commissioner of the Shanghai
Municipal Police and Divisional Officer, "A" Division, was
the only witness heard by the Court of Consuls yesterday in the
action in which Mr. Patrick J. Kelly, former detective-sergeant of
the S.M.P., represented by Mr. H. A. Reeks, is the petitioner and
the Shanghai Municipal Council is the defendant. Mr. Kelly claims
that he has been wrongfully dismissed from the force and that
the Council should pay him a sum of about £500 which he claims
is due him under the superannuation scheme, $3,546 which repres-
ent six months' pay, the money for the passages to England of
his wife and two children, court fees and $500.

Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, U.S. Consul-
General, presided and he was sup-
ported by Sir Herbert Phillips, H.M.
Consul-General, and Mr. Y. Miura,
Japanese Consul-General. Mr. R. T.
Bryan jun., represented the Shang-
hai Municipal Council. Mr. E. A.
Long, secretary of he Consular Body
was also present.
Before calling Mr. Robertson to
the witness box, Mr. Bryan handed
a cheque for $2,444.10 to counsel for
the petitioner, which money is due
to Mr. Kelly. After receiving the
court's assurances that the petitioner
could accept this money without pre-
judice to his case, it was accepted.
From the witness-box, Mr. Robert-
son told the court that on the after-
noon of March 31 or on the morning
of April 1, he told Mr. Kelly that
certain allegations of extortion had
been made against him. Witness
thereupon ordered Mr. J. Mason,
Divisional Detective Officer, to make
preliminary investigations into the
case.

Preliminary Investigations

After detailing at some length the
procedure adopted by the police in
cases of this nature, witness said that
according to the findings of these pre-
liminary investigations he drew up
certain charges against Mr. Kelly and
a number of Chinese detectives,
which were submitted to the respon-
dents by the officer in charge of Cen-
tral Station. The date for the hear-
ing was fixed for April 13, but re-
spondents were informed that wit-
ness was prepared to extend this
period if required.
In reply to a question, Mr. Robert-
son stated that police regulations did
not make it necessary for Mr. Kelly
to be present at the preliminary in-
vestigations and that Mr. Mason had
completed his report on April 9 or
10. The hearing, he added, com-
menced on April 13 and was com-
pleted on April 25, proceedings hav-
ing been carried on without interrup-
tion except for week-ends.
With reference to charges 4 and 5
of which both Mr. Kelly and the Chi-
nese detectives, according to the
wording of the procedure, were
found guilty, witness stated that Mr.
Kelly was only guilty of charge 4
but that both charges had been put
together as Mr. Kelly had left the
premises before the money was ex-
torted but that the Chinese had not
left, thus making it difficult to have
separate cases against Mr. Kelly and
the Chinese.

《字林西报》
264.7

前警署巡佐起诉工部局案

领事法庭听取分区主管证词；案件再次延期

上海公共租界工部局警务处助理处长兼“A”分区主管 H. D. M. 罗伯逊先生（Mr. H. D. M. Robertson）是昨日领事法庭在审理此案时传召的唯一证人。该案由原告、前上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探巡佐帕特里克·J·凯利先生（Mr. Patrick J. Kelly，由 H. A. 里克斯先生代表）提起，被告为上海公共租界工部局。凯利先生声称他被非法开除出警队，并要求工部局支付约500英镑，他声称这是根据养老金计划应付给他的款项；3,546美元，相当于六个月的薪水；其妻子和两个孩子返回英国的船费；诉讼费以及500美元。

美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯先生（Mr. Clarence E. Gauss）主持庭审，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦 Y. 先生（Mr. Y. Miura）列席支持。R. T. 布莱恩 junior 先生（Mr. R. T. Bryan jun.）代表上海公共租界工部局。领事团秘书 E. A. 朗先生（Mr. E. A. Long）亦在场。
在传唤罗伯逊先生出庭作证之前，布莱恩先生向原告辩护律师递交了一张金额为2,444.10美元的支票，该笔款项系欠付凯利先生。在得到法庭保证，即请愿人接受这笔钱不会损害其案件后，该支票被接受。
罗伯逊先生从证人席上告诉法庭，在3月31日下午或4月1日上午，他告诉凯利先生，有人对他提出了某些勒索指控。证人随即命令 J. 梅森先生（Mr. J. Mason，分区侦探主管）对该案进行初步调查。

初步调查

在详细阐述了警方在此类案件中采用的程序后，证人表示，根据这些初步调查的结果，他起草了针对凯利先生和数名华籍侦探的若干指控，这些指控由中央警署主管提交给被告方。听证日期定为4月13日，但已告知被告方，如有需要，证人准备延长此期限。
在回答一个问题时，罗伯逊先生表示，警务规章并未规定凯利先生必须出席初步调查，且梅森先生已于4月9日或10日完成了报告。他补充说，听证于4月13日开始，并于4月25日结束，除周末外，诉讼程序 uninterrupted（不间断）地进行。
关于第4和第5项指控，根据程序措辞，凯利先生和华籍侦探均被认定有罪，证人表示，凯利先生仅对第4项指控有罪，但这两项指控被合并在一起，因为凯利在勒索钱财发生前已离开现场，而华人并未离开，这使得难以针对凯利先生和华人分别立案。

Crime diaries, according to the
witness, were issued to all detectives
and to certain uniformed members of
the force so that their movements,
could be checked. He added that the
importance of the book may be seen
from the fact that they must be kept
for five years before being destroyed.
In reply to another question, witness
said that detectives were not strictly
required to fill out the crime diary
in full but that it was necessary to
state the time, the place visited and
the reason for the visit and that one
of the main purposes of the book was
to protect detectives against any
future allegations.

Motor Diaries

In dealing with the question of
motorcar diaries, witness said that
these had been introduced merely to
prevent detectives from using police
cars for private purposes and that
the diaries were checked daily by the
officer in charge of the station.
Asked whether it was customary
that a detective should dictate a re-
port to a clerk, Mr. Robertson said
that it was not, but that it was quite
usual for a detective to write out his
report in longhand and to let the
clerk type it out for him.
Mr. Kelly, according to witness,
was investigating a snatching case,
an attempted suicide case and a
trivial larceny on March 31. He had
also been requested to make out a
report on a shooting affair which oc-
curred on Szechuen Road Bridge and
to which he had been a witness.
Witness told the court that after
arrest and before discharge prisoners
must pass the officer on duty in the
charge room, it being considered
irregular when arrests or releases are
made in any other manner.
Pistols, Mr. Robertson went on to
say, must only be drawn when it is
believed that armed men are about to
be faced and when a foreign officer
draws his weapon the Chinese in his
party must do likewise.
Asked whether during the proceed-
ings against Mr. Kelly, witness had
called Mr. Tong, a lawyer represent-
ing one of the complainants at the
time, a liar as stated by Mr. Kelly
during a previous hearing in this
case. Mr. Robertson said that Tong
had come to give evidence with the
complainant and that he (witness)
did not call Tong a liar because he
could not use such language in the
presence of members of the force,
but that he had told the Chinese
lawyer that he had been guilty of un-
professional conduct, which fact
should be brought to the notice of
the Bar Association.
In referring to Mr. Kelly's super-
annuation funds, witness said that at
the time he had suggested that this
be paid out in full but that this sug-
gestion was turned down.
In cross-examining witness, Mr.
Reeks asked whether the record of
the proceedings against Mr. Kelly
were quite correct. Mr. Robertson re-
plied in the affirmative, adding that
he had taken everything down in
longhand himself. Mr. Reeks then
pointed out that in the record of his
findings, witness had stated that Mr.
Kelly and the Chinese detectives
were guilty of charges 4 and 5
whereas, a few minutes ago, he had
said that Mr. Kelly was only guilty
of charge 4.
Mr. Reeks then pointed out that
contrary to witness's assertion a few
minutes before, to the effect that all
investigation had been completed on
April 9 or 10, the statements of two
clerks were added on April 14 and
the very fact that something had
been added to charge at that time
showed that witness himself was not
fully conversant with the rules and
regulations of the Police Force. Mr.
Reeks added that only as a result of
the present case certain amendments
had been made to the regulations.

page_data.zh:
据证人称，犯罪日记（Crime diaries）发给所有警探以及警务处的部分穿制服人员，以便核查他们的行踪。他补充说，从这些日记在销毁前必须保存五年这一事实，即可看出其重要性。在回答另一个问题时，证人表示，虽然并不严格要求警探将犯罪日记填写得面面俱到，但必须注明时间、访问地点及访问原因，而该日记的主要目的之一是为了保护警探免受日后的任何指控。

机动车日记

在谈及机动车日记的问题时，证人表示，引入这种日记仅仅是为了防止警探将警车用于私人目的，并且这些日记由警署主管官员每日检查。当被问及警探向书记员口述报告是否属于惯例时，罗伯逊先生（Mr. Robertson）表示并非如此，但警探手写报告后让书记员打字誊清是很常见的做法。

据证人称，凯利先生（Mr. Kelly）在3月31日调查了一起抢夺案、一起自杀未遂案和一起轻微盗窃案。他还受命就发生在四川路桥（Szechuen Road Bridge）的一起枪击事件撰写报告，他是该事件的目击者。

证人告诉法庭，囚犯在被捕后、释放前，必须经过拘留室值班警官的检查，若以其他方式进行逮捕或释放则被视为违规。

罗伯逊先生接着说，只有在认为即将面对持械人员时才能拔出手枪；当外籍警官拔出武器时，其队伍中的华籍人员也必须同样拔出武器。

当被问及在对凯利先生的诉讼过程中，他是否如凯利先生在本案先前听证会上所述，曾称代表其中一名原告律师的童先生（Mr. Tong，音译）为骗子时，罗伯逊先生说，童先生是随原告一起来作证的，而他（证人）并没有称童先生为骗子，因为在警务处成员面前不能使用此类语言，但他确实告诉这位华籍律师，其行为有违职业操守，此事应提请律师公会注意。

在提及凯利先生的退休金基金时，证人表示，当时他曾建议全额支付这笔款项，但该建议被驳回。

在对证人进行交叉询问时，里克斯先生（Mr. Reeks）问针对凯利先生的诉讼记录是否完全准确。罗伯逊先生给予肯定回答，并补充说他亲自用长手写体记录了所有内容。随后，里克斯先生指出，在证人的裁决记录中，他陈述凯利先生和华籍警探在第4项和第5项指控上有罪，而在几分钟前，他却说凯利先生仅在第4项指控上有罪。

里克斯先生随后指出，与证人几分钟前声称所有调查已于4月9日或10日完成的说法相反，两名书记员的陈述是在4月14日补充进去的，而当时对指控有所增补这一事实本身就表明，证人本人对警务处的规章制度并不完全熟悉。里克斯先生补充说，正是由于本案，规章才做出了一些修订。

page_data.en:
264'5

Charges Considered Serious
Asked whether he considered the
charges against Mr. Kelly serious,
witness said that he considered them
very serious.
If this was the case, Mr. Reeks
added, why then did witness not
avail himself of the commissioner's
suggestion to appoint a board to hear
the case.
In reply, Mr. Robertson said that he
not only had sufficient evidence and
a clear case before him but that, if
the board had been appointed, he
would have headed it as president
and that consequently there would
have been no difference.
In referring to a statement made
by the witness earlier during the
afternoon to the effect that it was
very important that the crime diary
be filled out regularly, Mr. Reeks
asked witness whether he knew that
on the night of previous hearing a
detective attached to Chengtu Road
police station had not done so for 15
days and was told to complete it as
otherwise there could be trouble.
Mr. Robertson: "I still say it is an
important book."
Counsel for the petitioner then re-
ferred to the fact that in the records
of the proceedings which took place
before Mr. Robertson, under charges
4 and 5, there was not a shred of
evidence against Mr. Kelly showing
that either arms, ammunition of
opium were seized on the premises.
He also pointed out that both the
complainant and his wife had denied
that any pistol or ammunition was

Mr. Reeks then asked witness why,

wherever possible this is not done

sired publicity.
Counsel for the petitioner then

指控被视为严重

当被问及是否认为针对凯利先生的指控很严重时，证人表示他认为非常严重。

里克斯先生补充说，如果是这样，那么证人为何不采纳警务处处长的建议，任命一个委员会来审理此案。

对此，罗伯逊先生回答说，他不仅手头拥有充分的证据和清晰的案情，而且，如果任命了委员会，他将担任主席，因此结果不会有差别。

里克斯先生提到证人当天下午早些时候所作的陈述，即定期填写犯罪日记非常重要，据此他问证人是否知道，在前一次听证会当晚，成都路（Chengtu Road）警署的一名警探已有15天未填写日记，并被告知必须补全，否则会有麻烦。

罗伯逊先生：“我仍然说这是一本重要的簿册。”

申请人律师随后指出，在罗伯逊先生主持的、涉及第4项和第5项指控的诉讼记录中，没有任何证据显示凯利先生在现场缴获了武器、弹药或鸦片。他还指出，原告及其妻子均否认现场有任何手枪或弹药，证人对此表示同意。

里克斯先生随后问证人，既然罪行性质如此严重，为何未在华人法庭对华籍警探采取行动。证人表示，除非是极其严重的案件，否则尽可能不这样做，因为此类程序会引起不必要的公众关注。

申请人律师随后问证人，当囚犯就手枪和弹药作出陈述时，没有任何华籍警探对其进行交叉询问，这难道没有让他觉得，涉事华籍警探为了让自己不必面对华人法庭，而有牵连外国人的利益动机吗？

梅森先生（Mr. Mason）随后被传唤至证人席，但高斯先生（Mr. Gauss）建议休庭，由朗先生（Mr. Long）被任命为法庭专员，以听取更多证人的陈述。比扬先生（Mr. Biyan，音译）询问法庭是否准备驳回此案，得到的答复是法庭尚未准备好做出决定。

OCT 27 1939
20203

Former Police Sergeant's
Case Against Council

Hearing Again Adjourned in Court of Consuls; Questions
Of Extortion and Torture; Emphatic Denials

PATRICK J. Kelly, a former detective-sergeant attached to Central Station in the Shanghai Municipal Police, is at present living in Shanghai on money raised by subscriptions among his former colleagues in the Police Force. This was revealed yesterday afternoon in the Court of Consuls, where Kelly has brought an action against the Shanghai Municipal Council, his former employers, following his dismissal from the force. His legal fees. Kelly explained to the Court, had even been paid by the subscriptions, which provided him with $150 for his board and a little pocket money, and he had borrowed £20 from members of the force in order to pay his wife's and his children's passage back to England.

Kelly, whose case was heard by Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, U.S. Consul-General (presiding), Sir Herbert Phillips, H.M. Consul-General, and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General, claimed that he had been wrongfully dismissed from the police force and he asked that the Council should pay him a sum of £500 which, he stated, was the amount standing to his credit in the superannuation fund. He had been wrongfully deprived of this sum and also of $3,546 which represented six months' pay, he alleged. The petitioner further claimed that the Council should pay his wife's and his children's second-class passage money to England, Court fees and $500.

Mr. H. A. Reeks, who is representing Kelly, continued his examination from Tuesday afternoon. The Commissioner of Police in his report on petitioner's trial, he stated, had said that Kelly's letter to him of May 6 was an acknowledgment of an extortion plan. "You said in your appeal," said Mr. Reeks, addressing Kelly, "that the letter had been written on the suggestion of a superior officer."

Kelly agreed that the missive had been written on a senior officer's suggestion. The Divisional Officer, Mr H.D.M. Robertson, he said, had told him that he had seen Capt. Smyth, Deputy Commissioner, and had advised him to see the Deputy Commissioner himself or, better still, send his wife. Witness refused to send his wife and had a conversation with Capt. Smyth during which he told him that he was not guilty of the charges brought against him.

Pleading Letter

"Capt. Smyth said he would see what he could do with the Commissioner of Police. I waited and received information from Inspector Widdowson, who said that the Commissioner could not do anything," Kelly continued. Insp. Widdowson then asked him to write a pleading letter and witness agreed although he stated that he was not guilty of the third and fourth charges. After the letter had been written Mr. Widdowson asked him to put more pleading in the letter, which was drafted in pencil and typed out. Two paragraphs, which stated that his wife was with child at the time and that he would not appeal in connection with the case, were omitted.

Referring to a sentence in the letter which said "I admit I was incredibly foolish to be taken in by the Chinese detectives," Kelly told the Court that this did not mean an admission of knowledge of the extortion plan. In connection with the Commissioner's report upon Kelly's appeal, which stated that the evidence of the Chinese lawyer who represented the com-

possession of opium," petitioner continued. "Somebody in the charge-room was at fault. It was not my fault. I was not in the charge-room."

C.P.C. 1705 had stated, he went on, that two persons had been arrested and that the seized opium had been handed to Sub-Insp. Darters. The C.P.C. had added that he had noted down particulars of the two men and had handed them to Clerk Lee. The F.I.R., however, stated that only one person had been arrested, Kelly stated, and he did not know until later that a second man had been arrested. "If Sub-Insp. Darter's clerk had made the F.I.R. correctly I should have known that two people were arrested," said Kelly.

Sub-Insp. Darter had made a report that he had been informed that only one person had been arrested. At this point petitioner stated that he did not get this information and he had been accused of having released the man without the knowledge of the officer in the charge-room. He was stated to have done this to cover up something.

One of these detectives had been convicted of extortion. Witness, however, had no supervision over this man. 《字林西报》
1939年10月27日
20203

前警佐起诉工部局案

领事法庭再次休庭；涉及勒索与酷刑问题；坚决否认

帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly），上海公共租界工部局警务处中央巡捕房的前警佐，目前靠其在警务处的前同事募捐的资金在上海生活。昨天下午在领事法庭上揭示了这一情况，凯利在被警务处解职后，对其前雇主上海工部局提起了诉讼。凯利向法庭解释，他的法律费用甚至也是由捐款支付的，这些捐款为他提供了150美元的生活费和少量零用钱，他还向警务处成员借了20英镑，以支付其妻子和孩子返回英国的旅费。

凯利的案件由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss，主审）、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦义一（Y. Miura）审理。他声称自己被非法从警务处解职，并要求工部局支付他500英镑，他称这是他在退休金基金中的贷方余额。他声称自己被非法剥夺了这笔款项，以及相当于六个月薪水的3,546美元。申请人还要求工部局支付其妻子和子女返回英国的二等舱船票、法庭费用及500美元。

代表凯利的H·A·里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）继续周二下午开始的讯问。他指出，警务处处长在关于申请人审判的报告中称，凯利5月6日写给他的信是对勒索计划的承认。“你在上诉中说，”里克斯先生对凯利说，“那封信是在一位上级军官的建议下写的。”

凯利同意该信件是在一位高级军官的建议下写的。他说，分区警官H.D.M.罗伯逊先生（Mr H.D.M. Robertson）告诉他，自己已见过副警务处长史密斯上尉（Capt. Smyth），并建议他亲自去见副警务处长，或者更好的是，派他的妻子去。证人拒绝派他的妻子去，并与史密斯上尉进行了谈话，期间他告诉史密斯上尉，自己对针对他的指控无罪。

求情信

“史密斯上尉说他会看看警务处处长能做什么。我等待着，并从威多森督察（Inspector Widdowson）那里得到消息，说警务处处长无能为力，”凯利继续说道。威多森督察随后让他写一封求情信，证人同意了，尽管他声明自己对第三项和第四项指控无罪。信写好后，威多森先生让他在信中增加更多求情的内容，信件先用铅笔起草，然后打字誊清。其中两段被省略，这两段声称他的妻子当时怀有身孕，且他不会就此案提出上诉。

提到信中一句“我承认我被华籍警探欺骗是极其愚蠢的”，凯利告诉法庭，这并不意味着承认知晓勒索计划。关于警务处处长对凯利上诉的报告，该报告称代表原告的华籍律师的证词已被完整记录，且所有被告方均有充分权力听取该证词，申请人表示这不属实。

凯利声称，该人的证词受到干扰，且他（申请人）被勒令退出诉讼程序。在此阶段，里克斯先生指出，凯利可能只关心这些诉讼程序的十分之一，尽管如此，这还是进行了合并审理。市政律师R·T·布莱恩 junior 先生（Mr. R. T. Bryan, jun.）抗议里克斯先生是在辩论案情而不是提问。

被判勒索罪成立

凯利继续作证，他告诉法庭，在那起涉及的鸦片案中与他共事的华籍警探根本不受他管辖。其中一名警探已被判勒索罪成立。然而，证人对该人并无监管权。关于市政律师的报告，该报告称凯利“要么是勒索的同伙，要么知情”，申请人表示他并未被指控勒索。然而，他被警务处解职似乎表明他被认定犯有勒索罪，而市政律师的报告证实了这一点。

关于针对凯利的第一项指控，市政律师的报告明确指出逮捕了两名人员。“如果逮捕了两名人员，副督察达特斯（Sub-Insp. Darters，音译）会在初步调查报告（F.I.R.）中写明。报告说逮捕了一人，原因是

持有鸦片，”申请人继续说道。“拘留室里有人犯了错。这不是我的错。我不在拘留室里。”

他接着说，C.P.C. 1705（注：可能指某位华籍警员编号或职位缩写）曾陈述，有两人被捕，缴获的鸦片已交给副督察达特斯。该C.P.C.还补充说，他记下了这两人的详细信息并交给了李书记员（Clerk Lee）。然而，凯利陈述，初步调查报告（F.I.R.）却称只有一人被捕，他直到后来才知道第二个人也被捕了。“如果副督察达特斯的书记员正确制作了初步调查报告，我就应该知道有两个人被捕，”凯利说。

副督察达特斯曾报告说，他获悉只有一人被捕。此时申请人表示，他并未收到此信息，而他被指控在拘留室值班警官不知情的情况下释放了此人。据称他这样做是为了掩盖某些事情。

Translation Incorrect
Referring to a translation of a document written in Chinese by C.D.C. 260, who was the man who, with petitioner, released the prisoner from the charge-room, Kelly stated that the release of the man had been recorded in the Chinese detective's book and his (Kelly's) name was written at the bottom. The name, however, was only typed in at the bottom of the report. He did not make the entry.
Dealing with a copy of a written statement made by a Chinese detective found guilty of extortion, Kelly told the Court that he had not seen this document. The report had stated, "I saw Det.-Serg. Kelly and C.D.C. 260 bring a male Chinese to the Chinese detectives' office." This was untrue, Kelly stated, as he had returned to the station with C.D.C. 280 and had entered his own office. The report further alleged that C.D.C. 260 had found a parcel and a tin which Kelly had put in his pocket. The parcel was stated to have contained a pistol because the Chinese detained had overheard one detective tell another that it contained this article, petitioner stated. There had been a licence for a pistol but no weapon had been found in the house, he stated. The only man who had said that he had seized a pistol was the man who had been sentenced in the District Court.
When he had been suspended from duty, petitioner went to Insp. Duncan's office to surrender his pistol and at the time this convicted person was standing in the office. "When I surrendered my pistol, he probably thought that this was the pistol I had taken from Taku Road," Kelly told the Court. It was pointed out in the report that C.D.C. 260, when cross-examined by petitioner, had changed his statement. The report went on "I can only conclude that this was the result of pressure brought to bear on C.D.C. 260 by Kelly."

No Pressure
"I did not bring pressure to bear," said Kelly. I was not in a sufficiently important position to bring pressure to bear." Dealing with the report that complainant's wife seemed to be afraid of him, petitioner stated that the translation was incorrect. This person was, at times, given three or four minutes to think over her answers when they did not satisfy Mr. Robertson, he said. She had stated that she was afraid of all foreigners.
He added that when he was leaving the station on the opium case he was informed of an attempted suicide in Peking Road. When he got there the person had been removed to the General Hospital. Upon his return from the General Hospital he decided to proceed to Taku Road and C.D.C. 288 being with him at the time, he took him along in case he needed assistance. He added that he had been given no information about the attempted suicide and as it might have been a Chinese house he took the C.D.C. with him.
On the way to Taku Road the car stopped at the corner of Tiendong and Chekiang Roads and the C.D.C. got out for a moment or two to get a pair of overshoes as it was raining. No pistol or ammunition was seized nor was any opium found.

Cross-Examination
Cross-examined by Mr. Bryan, Kelly stated that he did not know that there would be a preliminary examination. He added that only one or two persons in the force read the Police Guide and Regulations. At this point Mr. Reeks questioned the interpretation of the rules. Kelly continued that he did not know that he was going to be charged on April 13 and he had been told that Mr. Robertson did not possess the right to try him.

译文有误

关于由华探 260 号（C.D.C. 260）所写的一份中文文件的译文，凯利（Kelly）指出，正是此人连同申请人一起将囚犯从候审室释放。凯利称，该男子的释放已记录在华探的登记簿中，且他（凯利）的名字签在底部。然而，该名字只是打印在报告底部的。他并未做此记录。

在处理一份被判定犯有勒索罪的华探所作的书面陈述副本时，凯利告诉法庭他未曾见过这份文件。报告中写道：“我看见凯利警佐和华探 260 号将一名中国男子带至华探办公室。”凯利称这不属实，因为他当时是与华探 280 号（C.D.C. 280）一同返回警局，并进入了他自己的办公室。报告进一步指控称，华探 260 号发现了一个包裹和一个铁罐，是凯利放入口袋中的。申请人称，据称该包裹内装有一把手枪，因为被拘留的中国人无意中听到一名侦探对另一名侦探说里面装有此物。他说，虽然有一张手枪执照，但在屋内并未发现武器。他说，唯一声称缴获手枪的人，是那位在地方法院被判刑的人。

当他被停职时，申请人前往邓肯（Duncan）督察的办公室上缴他的手枪，当时这名被定罪的人正站在办公室里。“当我上缴手枪时，他可能以为这就是我从大沽路（Taku Road）拿走的那把枪，”凯利告诉法庭。报告中指出，华探 260 号在接受申请人盘问时改变了他的证词。报告接着写道：“我只能得出结论，这是凯利对华探 260 号施加压力的结果。”

无施压行为

“我没有施加压力，”凯利说。“我的职位还不够重要，不足以施加压力。”针对报告中提到投诉人的妻子似乎害怕他的说法，申请人称译文有误。他说，当她的回答不能让罗伯逊（Robertson）先生满意时，有时会给她三四分钟的时间来思考答案。她曾表示她害怕所有外国人。

他补充说，当他因鸦片案离开警局时，有人告知他在北京路（Peking Road）发生了一起自杀未遂事件。当他到达那里时，那人已被送往广慈医院（General Hospital）。从广慈医院回来后，他决定前往大沽路，当时华探 288 号（C.D.C. 288）与他在一起，他便带上他以防需要协助。他补充说，他并未收到关于自杀未遂的任何信息，而且由于那可能是一户中国人家，他便带上了这名华探。

在前往大沽路的途中，汽车在天潼路（Tiendong Road）和浙江路（Chekiang Road）拐角处停下，华探下车一两分钟去买一双雨鞋套，因为当时正在下雨。没有缴获手枪或弹药，也没有发现鸦片。

交叉盘问

在布莱恩（Bryan）先生的交叉盘问下，凯利表示他不知道会有预审。他补充说，警队中只有一两个人阅读《警察指南》和规章。此时，里克斯（Reeks）先生对规则的解释提出了质疑。凯利继续说，他不知道自己在 4 月 13 日会被起诉，并且有人告诉他罗伯逊先生无权审判他。

当被问及他是否负责此案，以及两名华探是否在他的监督之下时，凯利给予了肯定的回答。“我向你提出，”布莱恩先生说，“你没有将前往大沽路的行程记入犯罪日记，是因为你不想让你的上级知道。”

里克斯先生随后插话说：“我很高兴进行重审。我们已经请求重审三次了。”

提及华探 260 号的陈述，该陈述称有两人被捕，凯利说这是一个错误，他不应为此负责。只有一人因持有鸦片被捕，另一人是作为嫌疑人被带来的。“为什么他没有出现在初步调查报告（F.R.R.）中？”布莱恩先生问道，“为什么他没有记入犯罪日记？”对此凯利回答说：“因为他没有出现在初步调查报告（F.I.R.）中，”里克斯反对布莱恩先生随后提出的说法，即该人是由凯利的助手非法逮捕的。

不知晓酷刑

申请人否认知晓对该男子施以酷刑。他说，副督察达特斯（Darters）是将初步调查报告（F.I.R.）和囚犯移交给华探，而不是交给他。在布莱恩先生提到囚犯声称遭受电刑后，凯利坚决否认知晓任何酷刑行为，并被领事法庭秘书 E. A. 朗（E. A. Long）先生要求控制自己的情绪。他在回答进一步的问题时补充道：“如果你要处理八九起刑事案件，你就无法完成所有这些文书工作。”

犯罪日记是由华人打字员打字的，他对此承担责任。他补充说，如果所有的警察命令都得到执行，就没有时间做其他工作了。

“我向你提出，你伪造了那份犯罪日记以掩盖你前往大沽路的事实，”布莱恩先生继续说道。“我没有。我把它记在了机动车日记里，”凯利回答道。

布莱恩先生接着说：“我向你提出，你将此人送交法庭是因为你想保护大沽路住所的居住者。”“是中国巡捕逮捕了他，不是我，”申请人回答道。他补充说，警队中很少有侦探按照规章规定撰写日记。“如果他们遵守规章，”他说，“他们会把所有时间都花在写日记上。”他随后提到了七名侦探，他们标记日记的方式与他的方法类似。

当被问及是否不觉得奇怪，所有去过大沽路的侦探都没有在日记中提到此事时，凯利表示他对其他人的行为不负责任。“你现在不觉得奇怪吗？”布莱恩先生问道，凯利回答说：“受审的是我吗？”在里克斯先生提出反对后，高斯（Gauss）先生评论说：“我认为这个问题提得不恰当。”

Legal Argument
"Did you expect armed robbers or
kidnappers in the place when you
went in the house with your pistol
out?" asked Mr. Bryan. "I didn't
know what to expect. After unloading
my pistol I put it back in my holster.
We found nothing at Taku Road,"
petitioner replied. He added that he
was not present when the man's wife
made a statement that something had
been found at the house. She had
retracted that statement later.
Asked if he had not written the
letter to the Commissioner because
he wanted his superannuation,
Kelly replied that this was not so.
He had not had a just enquiry. He
admitted writing, "I must plead for
the sake of my wife and children,
who will most suffer," but there had
been no admission of guilt. He
added that he thought he would drop
two or three months' seniority by
admitting some foolishness.
The case was adjourned after Mr.
Reeks had stated that he would like
to examine on several points raised
by his learned friend who had cover-
ed a most extraordinary piece of
ground in his cross-examination.
Mr. Bryan pointed out that he could
only examine on new points raised.
"That's just where you are wrong,"
replied Mr. Reeks, "I can only re-
examine on the old matter and not
the new." He denied that he was
mixing up British and American law
and said that it was the same in both
countries as far as he knew. Mr.
Bryan intimated that he had three
witnesses to call.

法律辩论

“当你持枪进入那所房子时，你预期会遇到武装抢劫犯或绑架者吗？”布莱恩先生问道。“我不知道会期待什么。卸下子弹后，我把枪放回了枪套。我们在大沽路什么也没发现，”申请人回答道。他补充说，当该男子的妻子作出声明称在屋内发现了某物时，他并不在场。她后来撤回了该声明。

当被问及他写信给总监是否是因为想要退休金时，凯利回答说并非如此。他没有得到公正的调查。他承认写过，“为了我的妻子和孩子，我必须恳求，他们将遭受最大的痛苦，”但这并不是承认有罪。他补充说，他认为承认一些愚蠢行为会使他的资历降低两三个月。

在里克斯先生表示他希望就其博学的朋友在交叉盘问中涉及的极不寻常的几个要点进行讯问后，案件休庭。布莱恩先生指出，他只能就新提出的要点进行讯问。“这正是你错的地方，”里克斯先生回答道，“我只能就旧事项进行再讯问，而不是新事项。”他否认自己混淆了英国法和美国法，并表示据他所知，两国在这方面的规定是一样的。布莱恩先生暗示他将传唤三名证人。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 27 1939

Kelly Damage
Suit Hearing
Is Continued

Ex-Detective Of S.M.P.
Cross-Examined In
Court Of Consuls

Patrick J. Kelly, dismissed Detective Sergeant of the Shanghai Municipal Police testified in his own behalf yesterday in his suit for recovery of $30,000 from the S.M.C now being heard before the Court of Consuls.

Chairman of the Court was American Consul-General Clarence Gauss aided by Sir Herbert Phillips, British Consul-General and Mr. Y Miura, Japanese Consul-General Mr. H. A. Reeks, Counsel for the petitioner, continued examination of his client from the opening session of the case held on Tuesday.

The hearing yesterday was given over to bringing out details of Mr Kelly's trial last spring when he was dismissed from the service, following investigation of his connection with an extortion case in which other members of the force were involved, and proof of his infraction of official regulations.

Legal Bickering

Mr. Reeks and the Municipal Advocate Mr. L. A. Bryan Jr., were involved through a large part of the proceedings yesterday in a caustic battle of words of wherein mutual objection to the others methods of examination and cross-examination broke down toward the end into an outspoken denunciation of each other's deplorable ignorance of the rules of re-examination.

In a two hour cross-examination Mr. Bryan dragged from Mr. Kelly the admission of some minor infractions of police regulations such as the negligence of police crime diary reports but that was about all that of a concrete nature he did get out of the petitioner.

On one particular report, the raid of a suspected narcotics den on Taku Road, Mr. Kelly had written in his diary that his whereabout at the time of raid was 'office'. Among other charges brought against him last spring were this statement; the unnecessary detention of a Chinese taken on suspicion of narcotics dealing during the raid and subsequently released without proper authority; wilfully making a false statement in his own detective diary, and failure to account for and return money, ammunition, pistol and opium allegedly taken at the Taku Road dwelling.

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）

1939 年 10 月 27 日

凯利损害赔偿
诉讼听证
继续进行

前上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探
在领事法庭接受交叉盘问

帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly），上海公共租界工部局警务处被开除的警佐，昨日在领事法庭审理的他向工部局（S.M.C.）索赔 30,000 美元的诉讼中为自己作证。

法庭主席是美国总领事克拉伦斯·高斯（Clarence Gauss），协助者包括英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦先生（Mr. Y Miura）。申请人的律师 H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生，从周二举行的案件开庭阶段起，继续对其当事人进行讯问。

昨天的听证会主要用于揭示去年春天凯利先生受审时的细节，当时他因涉及一起其他警队成员参与的勒索案的调查，以及被证实违反官方规章而被开除公职。

法律争执

里克斯先生和市公诉人 L. A. 布莱恩 Jr. 先生（L. A. Bryan Jr.）在昨天的大部分程序中卷入了一场激烈的唇枪舌战，双方相互指责对方的讯问和交叉盘问方法不当，最后在结束时演变为公然谴责对方对再讯问规则的无知令人遗憾。

在两小时的交叉盘问中，布莱恩先生从凯利先生口中逼出了一些轻微违反警察规章的行为，如警察犯罪日记报告的疏忽，但除此之外，他从申请人那里得到的具体实质内容寥寥无几。

关于一份特定的报告，即对大沽路一处疑似毒品窝点的突袭，凯利先生在日记中写道，突袭期间他的行踪是“办公室”。去年春天对他提出的其他指控包括：这一陈述；在突袭期间不必要地拘留了一名涉嫌毒品交易的中国男子，随后在未获适当授权的情况下将其释放；故意在自己的侦探日记中作虚假陈述；以及未能说明并归还在大沽路住所据称拿走的钱款、弹药、手枪和鸦片。

Ignorance Of Rules
For the most part, Mr. Kelly's
bland defense was lack of technical
knowledge of police regulations
which he said he had never read
because he knew what individual
rules made them up. He declared
hardly a police officer on the force
did more than shove the volume of
rules in a drawer and forget it.
As to the laxity of his subordinate
Chinese constables who had accompanied him on the Taku Road
venture and like him had thought
it too unimportant to report, Mr
Kelly would take no blame, saying
he could not take responsibility for
actions of others. Similarly he declared his blamelessness for inaccuracies in other reports made out by
his subordinates which he had
signed without reading.
To the question by Advocate
Bryan of whether he did not think
it strange that none of his men
had entered the Taku Road visit in
their diaries, Mr. Kelly asked coolly:
"Am I on trial?"
Mr. Kelly stated he was primarily
interested in clearing his name and
secondarily in receiving the compensation due him. It was with this
vindication in mind that he wrote
the Commissioner of Police a letter
last spring asking for the allotment
of his super-annuation of which
dismissal had deprived him.

Claims Injust Trial
Although adamant on the injustice of his trial which he said he
had believed at the time was an
inquiry, Mr. Kelly declared he had
not mentioned the matter in his
letter because he wanted to get on
the right side of the official.
Abruptly concluding his cross-examination of the petitioner which
had previously told the court might
drag on considerably longer, Mr.
Bryan said he would have three new
witnesses at the next hearing of
the case
Mr. Reeks said he might have to
do some re-examining of the witnesses next time. The two legal experts then fell out on the point of
whether it would be possible to re-examine as no new evidence had
been produced during Mr. Bryan's
cross-examination. Mr. Reeks yielded.
The court rose and Mr. Gauss said
he would inform both counsel of
the date of next sitting.

对规则的无知

凯利先生平淡的辩护主要在于缺乏对警察规章的技术性知识，他说他从未读过这些规章，因为他知道构成规章的各个具体规则。他宣称，警队中几乎没有警官会去做更多的事，只不过是把那本规章塞进抽屉里然后就忘了。

至于陪同他进行大沽路行动的下属中国巡捕的松懈态度，他们也像他一样认为此事太不重要而不值得报告，凯利先生不愿承担任何责任，称他不能为他人的行为负责。同样，他宣称自己对下属制作的其他报告中的不准确之处无罪，尽管他在未阅读的情况下签署了这些报告。

面对公诉人布莱恩关于是否不觉得奇怪他的手下都没有在日记中记录大沽路之行的提问，凯利先生冷静地问道：“受审的是我吗？”

凯利先生表示，他主要感兴趣的是洗清自己的名声，其次是获得应得的补偿。正是出于这种平反昭雪的考虑，他于去年春天写信给警务总监，要求分配因被开除而剥夺的退休金。

声称审判不公

尽管凯利先生坚持认为他的审判是不公正的——他说他当时认为那只是一次调查——但他宣称他在信中没有提及此事，因为他想站在官员有利的一边。

布莱恩先生突然结束了对申请人的交叉盘问，此前他曾告诉法庭盘问可能会持续更长时间，他说在下一次案件听证会上他将带来三名新证人。

里克斯先生说下次他可能需要对一些证人进行再讯问。随后，两位法律专家就在布莱恩先生的交叉盘问期间未产生新证据的情况下是否可以进行再讯问这一点上发生了分歧。里克斯先生做出了让步。

法庭休庭，高斯先生表示他将通知双方律师下一次开庭的日期。

《上海泰晤士报》。
1938年10月27日

律师间的激烈争执
成为前工部局警长案件焦点

帕特里克·J·凯利先生遭受工部局律师的严厉盘问；
著名罪案日记中的记录

勒索案中被指寻找替罪羊

昨天下午，在领事法庭举行的听证会上，前上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）警务处警长帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）起诉上海公共租界工部局一案成为焦点，双方律师发生激烈争执，凯利遭受了严厉的盘问。凯利要求追回30,000元养老金、相当于六个月薪水的代通知金，以及他和家人返回英国的二等舱船票，并由被告承担诉讼费用。该案由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）主持，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦义一（Y. Miura）组成的领事法庭审理。在代表工部局辩护的工部局律师R·T·布莱恩（R. T. Bryan）表示将在下次听证时传唤三名警方证人后，案件无限期休庭。凯利先生在作证结束时声明，他是为了荣誉而战，而非为了金钱。

昨天，布莱恩先生对凯利先生进行了严厉的盘问，期间偶尔被凯利的代理律师H·A·里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生的爆发所打断，里克斯先生多次抗议对方律师的提问方式。在某一个阶段，里克斯先生抗议道：“法官阁下，证人的思维曲折是有限的。”在布莱恩先生连珠炮般的质问过程中，凯利先生显得不如第一次听证时那样镇定，被法庭书记员要求控制情绪。在另一个阶段，凯利先生问布莱恩先生，他（凯利）是否正在受审。

工部局律师还对里克斯先生频繁的异议表示不满，有一次抗议道：“里克斯先生，当你提问时，尽管是诱导性问题，我并没有提出异议；因此当我提问时，你也不应提出异议。”

非同寻常的程序

里克斯先生有一次将布莱恩先生的盘问形容为“最非同寻常的程序，试图让我的客户为其下属在警务处的行为负责。”布莱恩先生在关于凯利未能遵守某些警务规定的盘问中反驳凯利道：“你说的是道听途说，是从你听到的内容中拼凑出来的，而不是来自你从未阅读过的《警务规章》。”凯利则辩称，警务处中没有两名警官是严格遵守规章的。在盘问过程中，凯利声明他是为了荣誉而战，并告知法庭，他靠警务处一些成员提供的资金生活，他说他是从这些人那里借钱送妻儿回英国的。他说甚至连他的零花钱也是由他们提供的。他承认自己在未遵守警务规则方面犯了技术性错误，但强调自己并非故意或有意为之。

在工部局提交给法庭的答辩状中，工部局律师指出，凯利因以下四个原因被“开除”出警务处：1. 在警务处的第一本罪案日记这一官方文件中 knowingly（明知故犯地）作出虚假陈述；2. 在不必要地拘留一名华人后，未经值班警官知晓和同意便不当将其释放；3. 在其个人侦探日记中故意作出虚假和误导性陈述；4. 未能说明并归还他从大沽路（Taku Road）某弄堂房屋中拿走的钱款、手枪、弹药和鸦片。在第一次听证时，证人对他由上级警官就列出的四项指控进行“审判”的方式提出异议。昨天布莱恩先生就此次审判对他进行长时间盘问时，证人坚持称据他所知这仅是一次调查，里克斯先生插话道：“我的博学的朋友正在再次审判他，我很高兴有机会这样做。我很高兴能对本案进行重审。我们曾三次要求重审，但他们（警务处）没有批准。你们正在再次定罪一个人……”布莱恩先生简短地评论说，此人已被定罪。

在昨天的程序开始时，里克斯先生花了半小时完成对申请人的讯问，申请人被问及……（原文此处似乎有OCR错误或文本断裂，结合下文语境及p32开头，此处应为过渡句，但原文p31末尾与p32开头衔接处存在重复或错乱，依原文翻译如下：）……你们声称这些款项是欠你们的。工部局曾提供给你们一笔小额款项？

page_data.en:
Living On Subscriptions
Witness: "$2.400 my own sub-
scriptions to the Fund. I refused
it, Sir, and lived on subscriptions
made by various members of the
Force, who even paid my legal
fees. I have no money at all. They
pay $150 for my board and give me
a few dollars for my pocket money.
I had to borrow £20 from a mem-
ber of the Force to send my wife
and children back to England, and
I still owe the money."
Mr. Kelly, in reply to Mr. Bryan,
stated that he was not notified on
March 31, last, by Assistant Police
Commissioner Robertson, that his
conduct was under suspicion. He
was suspended by Inspector Duncan.
He knew that his conduct was the
subject of investigation. He did
not know at the time about any
preliminary inquiry being held.
Mr. Bryan: "You always had the
Shanghai Municipal Guide and Re-
gulations?"—"Yes. I have had a
copy for some time."
"Did you read it?"—Witness re-
plied that no two policemen in the
Force read it. He did not know
what it was made up from.
"Doesn't it contain definite in-
structions as to what a police officer
had to carry out, and you didn't
read it?"—"I didn't think that was
necessary."
Mr. Bryan pointed out to witness
at this stage that the instructions
stated, inter alia, that an officer
shall be suspended from duty when
there were grounds leading the
Police to believe that he had com-
mitted infractions of regulations
which might lead to preferment of
charges against him, eventually
leading to his dismissal or major
punishment.

Mr. Reeks Objects
Counsel then pointed out to
witness that according to the fore-
going, his suspension from duty
would imply that a preliminary in-
quiry was being held. Witness re-
plied with "It would be held." Mr.
Reeks objected on the ground that
these questions were not fair.
Further questions ensued and
witness stressed that he objected to
his "trial," declaring that the senior
officer trying him had no authority
to do so.
The cross-examination then took
the following course:
Mr. Bryan: "What you say is
hearsay picked up here and there
and not according to Police Regula-
tions, is that it?—From my experi-
ence in the Force, Sir.
Not from the Regulations please
answer 'Yes' or 'No.'—No.
In other words, you didn't read
the regulations at all?—I looked it
up during my suspension from duty.
You thought there was a prelim-
inary inquiry, when it was a trial?
—No, I thought it was an inquiry.
It was not a trial, to me.
Now, let's come to the first charge
against you, Mr. Kelly. When the
First Information Report (FIR) was
referred to you, you become an
officer in charge of a case—Yes. I
handled the case.
The Chinese detectives under you
were your subordinates?—Yes
They had to take your instructions
and were subordinate to you?—Yes.
The primary purpose of the FIR
is to give your superior officer in-
formation and not for the Muni-
cipal Advocate to prosecute the
case?—It is for the Municipal Ad-
vocate.
Principally, though, for your
superior officers, yes or no?—For the
Municipal Advocate for the issuing
of charges.
But before charging, for your
superior officers?—Yes.
Any everything you put in your
crime diary, your superior officers
must know. They must initial it?
—Yes.
Famous Crime Diary
Handing witness a book, counsel
went on:
page_data.zh:
靠捐款生活

证人：“2,400美元是我自己向基金的捐款。我拒绝了，先生，而是靠警务处各种成员提供的捐款生活，他们甚至支付了我的法律费用。我身无分文。他们为我支付150元的伙食费，并给我几美元作为零花钱。我不得不向一名警务处成员借了20英镑，以便送我的妻儿回英国，而我至今仍欠着这笔钱。”

凯利先生在回答布莱恩先生时表示，去年3月31日，副警务总监罗伯逊（Robertson）并未通知他其行为受到怀疑。他是被督察邓肯（Duncan）停职的。他知道自己的行为正在接受调查。但他当时并不知道正在进行任何初步调查。

布莱恩先生：“你一直拥有《上海市政指南及规章》？”——“是的。我持有一份副本已有一段时间。”

“你读过吗？”——证人回答说，警务处中没有两名警察会去读它。他不知道它是由什么构成的。

“它不包含关于警察必须执行的具体指令吗，而你却没有阅读？”——“我认为那没有必要。”

在此阶段，布莱恩先生向证人指出，指令中规定，除其他事项外，当有理由使警方相信某警官违反了可能导致对其提出指控、最终导致其被解雇或受到重大处罚的规定时，该警官应被停职。

里克斯先生提出异议

随后，律师向证人指出，根据上述规定，他的停职意味着正在进行初步调查。证人回答说：“应该是这样的。”里克斯先生以这些问题不公平为由提出反对。

接着进行了进一步的提问，证人强调他反对对他的“审判”，宣称审判他的高级警官无权这样做。

随后的盘问过程如下：

布莱恩先生：“你说的是道听途说，是从各处拼凑起来的，并不符合《警务规章》，是吗？”——“基于我在警务处的经验，先生。”

请不要依据经验，请回答“是”或“否”。——“否。”

换句话说，你根本没有阅读过规章？——“我在停职期间查阅过。”

你以为那是初步调查，而实际上那是审判？——“不，我以为那是调查。对我来说，那不是审判。”

现在，让我们来看看对你的第一项指控，凯利先生。当首份情报报告（FIR）转交给你时，你就成为了案件的负责警官——“是的。我处理了该案。”

你手下的华捕侦探是你的下属？——“是的。”

他们必须听从你的指令并隶属于你？——“是的。”

首份情报报告的主要目的是向你的上级警官提供信息，而不是为了让工部局律师起诉案件？——“是为了工部局律师。”

但主要是为了你的上级警官，是还是否？——“是为了工部局律师签发指控。”

但在提出指控之前，是为了你的上级警官？——“是的。”

你在罪案日记中记录的任何内容，你的上级警官都必须知晓。他们必须 initials（签署缩写名/草签）确认？——“是的。”

著名的罪案日记

律师递给证人一本簿子，继续说道：

page_data.en:
Let us look at this famous crime
diary. Why did you put in there
'Office' when you have gone to
Taku Road? Witness replied that
although he signed the diary, he
was not responsible for its compila-
tion.
But you signed it and were re-
sponsible for it?—Technically, yes.
Counsel suggested to witness that
this entry was made because he did
not want his superior officers to
know that he had gone to the
address in Taku Road. Witness
replied that his visit there was men-
tioned in the motor car book kept
by the Force. Counsel pointed out
that this book was not for the record
of the superior officers about whom
he was quizzing witness.
Mr. Bryan later on suggested to
witness that one of his assistants
had made an illegal arrest. Mr.
Reeks objected to the question.
After protracted questioning of
witness regarding "trivial inquiries"
made by him into police cases or
"petty cases," Mr. Bryan followed
with:
You falsified the crime diary?—
No.
You falsified it intentionally?—
No.
After witness had declared that
there was no need for him to make
the entry in the diary regarding his
visit to Taku Road because, as he
explained, nothing was found and
there would be no charges prefer-
red against anyone, Mr. Bryan ask-
ed: "You mean it is your own
opinion only that there is no need
to put it in the crime diary although
the Police Regulations say you must
do so?—The regulations are not
strictly adhered to.
Extortion By Police
In reply to further questions put
by Mr. Bryan, witness said he had
no knowledge at the time about a
certain extortion case in which it
was disclosed several members of
the Force were involved, and sub-
sequently dismissed. A Chinese, ac-
cording to the records, had been ar-
rested and given a term of impri-
sonment.
Mr. Bryan: You sent this man as
a scapegoat to the Court so that
you could protect the man in Taku
Road?—Witness entered a denial,
explaining that the so-called 'scape-
goat' had not been arrested by him
but by a Chinese constable.
He was tortured with electricity
by your assistants?—Not that I
know of. The Chinese constable,
and not me, arrested him.
Counsel pointed out to witness
that the constable was his sub-
ordinate. Witness denied counsel's
suggestion that he did not report
the man's release to his superiors.
Mr. Bryan proceeded to read to
Mr. Kelly Police Regulations, an
important part of which, according
to counsel, was that it was the
duty of police officers to record
their actions in diaries with which
they were supplied. Witness stated
that no detective ever wrote up his
diary regularly. That would entail
hours of writing. In his case, it
would take two hours each day.
Instructions Disregarded
You never carried out the in-
structions? Mr. Bryan next asked
witness. After witness replied that
no detective in the Force strictly
carried out the particular instruc-
tions, Mr. Bryan remarked to him:
Then, according to you, no detec-
tive in the Force ever carries out
instructions and you were probably
the only one who did?—I didn't say
so.
Asked to name any police officers
he knew who did not carry out
these instructions implicitly, wit-
ness gave several names of mem-
bers of the Force who, he said, he
had worked with, including officers
in the Bubbling Well Road district.
Witness explained that these offi-
cers did not enter their diaries,
according to the rules laid down by
the Police Commissioner.
page_data.zh:
让我们看看这本著名的罪案日记。既然你去了大沽路，为什么在里面写上‘办公室’（Office）？证人回答说，虽然他签署了日记，但他不负责其编制。

但你签署了它并对此负责？——“技术上来说，是的。”

律师暗示证人，之所以这样记录，是因为他不希望上级警官知道他曾前往大沽路的地址。证人回答说，他的那次访问在警务处保存的汽车日志中有提及。律师指出，这本日志并不是用于向他正在询问证人的那些上级警官汇报记录的。

后来，布莱恩先生向证人暗示，他的一名助手进行了非法逮捕。里克斯先生对该问题提出反对。

在对证人就其对警方案件或“小案”进行的“琐碎调查”进行了长时间的盘问后，布莱恩先生接着问道：

你伪造了罪案日记？——“没有。”

你是故意伪造的吗？——“没有。”

在证人声明没有必要在日记中记录他访问大沽路一事，因为他解释说当时未发现任何情况，也不会对任何人提出指控后，布莱恩先生问道：“你的意思是，尽管《警务规章》规定你必须这样做，但仅凭你个人的意见认为没有必要记入罪案日记？——“规章并没有被严格遵守。”

警方勒索

在回答布莱恩先生提出的进一步问题时，证人表示，当时他对某起勒索案并不知情，该案后来披露警务处几名成员卷入其中并被解雇。根据记录，一名华人被捕并被判处监禁。

布莱恩先生：“你把这个人当作替罪羊送上法庭，以便保护大沽路的那个人？”——证人予以否认，解释说所谓的“替罪羊”并非由他逮捕，而是由一名华捕逮捕的。

他被你的助手用电刑折磨？——“据我所知并非如此。逮捕他的是那名华捕，而不是我。”

律师向证人指出，该名警员是他的下属。证人否认了律师关于他未向上级报告该人获释情况的暗示。

布莱恩先生接着向凯利先生宣读《警务规章》，据律师称，其中重要的一部分是，警官有义务在使用配发的日记本中记录他们的行动。证人表示，从来没有侦探定期撰写日记。那将需要花费数小时书写。就他而言，每天需要花费两个小时。

无视指令

“你从未执行过这些指令？”布莱恩先生接着问证人。在证人回答说警务处中没有侦探严格执行该特定指令后，布莱恩先生对他说道：“那么，按照你的说法，警务处中没有侦探执行指令，而你可能是在执行的唯一一人？”——“我没这么说。”

当被要求列举他所知的任何未完全执行这些指令的警官姓名时，证人列举了几名警务处成员的姓名，他说他曾与他们共事，包括静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）地区的警官。证人解释说，这些警官并未按照警务总监制定的规则填写日记。

page_data.en:
Mr. Bryan: In the case we men-
tioned, not a single detective men-
tioned in their diary that they had
gone to Taku Road. Don't you think
that is strange?—I am not respon-
sible for the actions of other
people.
Don't you think it strange, I ask-
ed?—Am I on trial? witness re-
plied.
Counsel went on to dwell on
various things mentioned in the
record of the investigation into
petitioner's conduct and read part
of a letter which a Chinese com-
plainant in a certain case had sent
his wife stating that he would re-
turn to Shanghai if his spouse
would guarantee his safety. Coun-
sel suggested that the man was
threatened.
Mr. Bryan: "Possibly by you and
possibly by the Chinese detective?"
—Witness emphatically denied the
charge. Witness also denied Mr.
Bryan's suggestion that he had
threatened the man to get him out
of town so that the Police could
not proceed with the case.

Worried About His Character
An "appeal" which Mr. Kelly
was stated to have sent to the Police
Commissioner when an inquiry into
his conduct was conducted next
was the subject of protracted ques-
tioning by Mr. Bryan. Counsel sug-
gested to witness the reason for
the appeal was that witness hoped
that he would mollify the Commis-
sioner and get his superannuation
fund. "No!" declared witness, "it
was my character that I was wor-
ried about, my honour comes
before any money.
Mr. Kelly agreed with Mr. Bryan
that had the recommendations of
Mr. Robertson, Assistant Commis-
sioner, been followed by the Com-
missioner, he would have got his
superannuation fund in full. Wit-
ness negatived counsel's suggestion,
however, that he would then
have been satisfied and declared
that he would still have fought the
case. He admitted that his written
appeal to the Commissioner was
not elicited by duress, torture or
force, but that he had signed it of
his own free will. Asked why he
had not considered it advisable to
put other vital matters in the ap-
peal, witness explained that that
would be tantamount to fighting
the Commissioner.
Asked why he had mentioned in
his appeal that he had been in-
credibly foolish on account of
Chinese detectives, witness stated
that that had been suggested to
him for insertion by another offi-
cer. He thought he would be ad-
judged guilty only of minor in-
fractions and denied counsel's
suggestion that he expected to get
off altogether and receive his
superannuation fund in its entirety.
In reply to further questions,
witness admitted that prior to the
inquiry he did not claim that Mr.
Robertson had been prejudiced
against him. Mr. Bryan suggested
that, in fact, witness did not claim
Mr. Robertson was prejudiced until
the trail was over and judgment
rendered against him. Witness
said he ascertained that this officer
was prejudiced against him during
the trial. Witness, in reply to
further questions, declared that the
written appeal to the Commissioner
had been drafted out for him and,
repeated that he had left something
out 'because he was not fighting
the Commissioner.' He said he was
told to write a pleading letter.
page_data.zh:
布莱恩先生：在我们提到的那个案件中，没有一名巡捕在其日记中提到他们曾去过大沽路。你不觉得这很奇怪吗？——我不对别人的行为负责。
我问你，你不觉得奇怪吗？——证人回答说：“我是在受审吗？”
辩护律师继续详述调查申请人行为记录中提到的各种事项，并宣读了一封信的部分内容，该信是某案件中的一名中国投诉人写给其妻子的，信中称如果其配偶能保证他的安全，他将返回上海。辩护律师暗示此人受到了威胁。
布莱恩先生：“可能是被你，也可能是被那名华籍巡捕？”——证人坚决否认了这一指控。证人还否认了布莱恩先生的暗示，即他威胁此人将其赶出城，以便警方无法继续处理该案。

担心自己的名誉
据称，凯利先生在对他的行为进行调查时，曾向警务处处长提交了一份“申诉”，这成为布莱恩先生长时间盘问的主题。辩护律师向证人暗示，提出申诉的原因是证人希望以此安抚处长，从而获得他的养老金。“不！”证人宣称，“我担心的是我的名誉，我的荣誉高于任何金钱。”
凯利先生同意布莱恩先生的说法，即如果处长采纳了助理处长罗伯逊先生的建议，他本可以全额获得养老金。然而，证人否定了辩护律师的暗示，即他当时会感到满意，并宣称他仍会对该案进行抗争。他承认，他写给处长的书面申诉并非出于胁迫、折磨或武力，而是出于自愿签署。当被问及为何认为不宜在申诉中列入其他重要事项时，证人解释说，那将等同于与处长对抗。
当被问及为何在申诉中提到自己因华籍巡捕而变得极其愚蠢时，证人表示，这是另一名警官建议他加入的内容。他认为自己只会被判定犯有轻微违规行为，并否认了辩护律师的暗示，即他期望完全脱罪并全额领取养老金。
在回答进一步的问题时，证人承认，在调查之前，他并未声称罗伯逊先生对他存有偏见。布莱恩先生暗示，事实上，证人直到审判结束并作出对他不利的判决后，才声称罗伯逊先生存有偏见。证人说，他是在审判期间发现这名警官对他存有偏见的。证人在回答进一步的问题时宣称，写给处长的书面申诉是由他人代为起草的，并重申他遗漏了一些内容，“因为他不想与处长对抗”。他说，有人告诉他写一封求情信。

page_data.en:
Preferential Treatment
Witness went on to say that, in his opinion, Mr. Robertson was not empowered to try him. He should have been tried before a board. Mr. Bryan then asked him: "So you think that, being a foreigner, you were entitled to special privileges?" Witness replied that the same regulations did not apply to Chinese members of the Force.
Mr. Bryan: You claim preferential treatment because you are a foreigner? Is that your reason for this case? Witness repeated that he thought he should be tried by a proper board. Mr. Bryan then referred witness to police regulations, where it was stated that foreigner may ask for trial before a board. The regulations, counsel pointed out, did not state that the foreigner was entitled to such a trial. Witness remarked that, in his opinion, he should have been present at the preliminary trial.
Mr. Bryan: In other words, you thought a preliminary inquiry was like a preliminary hearing before a British court, where a magistrate sits?—I should have been present.
Mr. Bryan, after challenging witness to point out to him in regulations where his presence was imperative, suggested that the presence of a defendant in preliminary inquiries was not necessary. Witness countered by saying that he was being disciplined, not charged as a criminal. Counsel stressed that this was all the more reason why his presence was unnecessary.
The cross-examination being concluded, Mr. Reeks declared that Mr. Bryan had covered an extraordinary piece of ground, but was apparently unacquainted with what transpired at the trial of his client and, for this reason, counsel wanted to re-examine his witness.
Battle Over Legal Procedure
A legal battle ensued, Mr. Bryan objecting to the re-examination on the ground that he had not brought out any new matter to entitle the opposition to re-examine witness. If such re-examinations were allowed, counsel declared, the case would go on indefinitely. Mr. Reeks countered by saying that, in his opinion, his learned friend had got his idea of procedure reversed. Mr. Bryan followed up by declaring that Mr. Reeks apparently was following the British rule of procedure. Mr. Reeks asserted that it was the rule in every country. After a sharp exchange, Mr. Reeks said: "I will leave my case here. I will not need any re-examination."
Before the adjournment, the President of the Court intimated that both counsel would be notified of the next session.
page_data.zh:
优待
证人接着说，在他看来，罗伯逊先生无权审判他。他本应由一个委员会进行审判。布莱恩先生随后问他：“所以你认为，因为你是外国人，你就享有特权？”证人回答说，同样的规定并不适用于警队的华籍成员。
布莱恩先生：你声称因为你是外国人而享有优待？这就是你提起本案的理由吗？证人重申，他认为他应由一个适当的委员会进行审判。布莱恩先生随后向证人提及警务规章，其中规定外国人可以要求在委员会面前受审。辩护律师指出，规章并未规定外国人有权要求此类审判。证人 remarked 说，在他看来，他本应出席初步审讯。
布莱恩先生：换句话说，你认为初步调查就像英国法院由治安法官主持的初步听证会？——我本应在场。
布莱恩先生在要求证人在规章中指出何处规定他必须在场后，暗示被告出席初步调查并非必要。证人反驳说，他受到的是纪律处分，而非作为刑事罪犯被起诉。辩护律师强调，这更是他无需在场的理由。
交叉询问结束后，里克斯先生宣布，布莱恩先生涵盖了极广的范围，但显然不了解其客户在审判过程中发生的情况，因此，辩护律师希望重新询问他的证人。

法律程序之争
随之展开了一场法律争论，布莱恩先生反对重新询问，理由是他并未提出任何新事项使对方有权重新询问证人。辩护律师宣称，如果允许此类重新询问，案件将无限期拖延下去。里克斯先生反驳说，在他看来，他的博学朋友搞错了程序顺序。布莱恩先生紧接着宣称，里克斯先生显然遵循的是英国的程序规则。里克斯先生断言，这是每个国家的规则。经过一番激烈的交锋，里克斯先生说：“我就在此结束我的案件。我不需要任何重新询问。”
在休庭前，法庭庭长暗示，两位辩护律师都将收到下次开庭的通知。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
OCT 25 1939
Former Detective-Sergeant
Sues Municipal Council
Wrongful Dismissal Alleged ; £500 Claimed from
Superannuation Fund ; Question of Pistol Seizure

A FORMER detective-sergeant of the Shanghai Municipal Police, attached to Central Police Station, Patrick J. Kelly, appeared as petitioner before the Court of Consuls yesterday afternoon in an action against the Shanghai Municipal Council. Kelly claimed that he had been wrongfully dismissed from the force and he asked that the Council should pay him a sum of about £500 which, he stated, was the amount standing to his credit in the superannuation fund.
He had been wrongfully deprived of this sum and also of $3,546 which represented six months' pay, he alleged.
The petitioner further claimed that the Council should pay his, his wife's and his children's second-class passage money to England, court fees and $500. Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, U.S. Consul-General, presided and he was supported by Sir Herbert Phillips, H.M. Consul-General, and Mr. Y. Miura, Japanese Consul-General.

Kelly was represented by Mr. H. A. Reeks of Messrs. Ellis & Hays, while Mr. R. T. Bryan jun., Municipal Advocate, appeared on behalf of the Shanghai Municipal Council. Mr. E. A. Long, Secretary of the Court of Consuls, was also present.
Before calling on Kelly to give evidence Mr. Reeks stated that this was not a trial as to whether petitioner was guilty of the charges with which he had been charged but that the Council had acted in an irregular manner, even high-handed manner, in terminating his employment and taking away monies which were his.
At this point Mr. Bryan handed to the Court a record of the original trial of Kelly, the report of the trial officer, the report of the Municipal Advocate, the petitioner's personal diary and the Shanghai Municipal Police Guide and Regulations.
"After a man has been proved guilty of not having made a report of the seizure of a pistol and ammunition the thing is to prove that the pistol and ammunition were, in fact, seized," Mr. Reeks stated. "Was there a pistol and ammunition seized?" he asked.

Report Inaccurate
Kelly was then sworn and Mr. Reeks explained to the Court that, although it might transpire that petitioner would make an attack on one or two persons, he was in Court to re-establish his own credit.
Petitioner told the court that he was born in Carlisle, England, and that he had been engaged by the Shanghai Municipal Police in London on October 3, 1929. He had been given the Terms of Employment together with a copy of King's Regulations which, he was told, would be applicable to him. He received his letter of appointment in Shanghai.
He began service in Shanghai on November 11, 1929, the appointment being confirmed by the letter of appointment in August 1931. Later he had been faced with four charges which amounted to breaches of discipline. On two of these he had pleaded technically, but not wilfully guilty.
The report of the police proceedings against him, he said, had been taken down by the Divisional Officer, Assistant Commissioner H.D.M. Robertson. This report was inaccurate, some questions which were asked and answered, not being included. There had also been alterations, he said.

Loss of $30,000
At the time he faced these charges there were also charges against other police officers, some of them having been accused of extortion of money. He had been found guilty of having been concerned in the extortion and he had received a most severe punishment. This had caused a loss to him of more than $30,000.
Petitioner continued that he was married and had two children; who had sailed to England with his wife. He had stayed behind to fight this case but it was his intention to return to England where he had served in the Territorial Army.
There had been no preliminary enquiry, Kelly stated, and he was first questioned by Mr. Robertson at what was called his trial. He had been told by senior members of the Force that Mr. Robertson did not possess the right to try him and that a court should consist of a divisional officer and two superintendents. In the first place when he was questioned by Mr. Robertson, Supt. Mason had been present.

Drawers Searched
He had been asked if he had paid a visit to Taku Road on March 30 in connection with an opium case. Asked why he had not mentioned this visit in his diary Kelly replied that he did not think it was necessary as he had reported it in the motor car diary. After the questioning he left the room and half an hour later he was informed that he had been suspended from duty, his drawers were searched and he was told to hand over his pistol and warrant card.
On April 11 a list of charges was handed to him and a number of statements made by various people were handed to him. He was told to hand the statements to Chinese detectives for them to read.
Mr. Reeks then dealt with the first and third charges against Kelly which were that he had knowingly made and signed a false statement in an official document, First Crime Diary, F.I.R. 821, and that on March 30, at Central Station, he had made a false and untrue statement in his detective's diary book. At this point Mr. Reeks pointed out that the latter document was nothing more than a duty roster.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，
1939年10月25日
前巡佐
起诉工部局
指控非法解雇；从养老金中索赔500英镑；涉及手枪没收问题

上海公共租界工部局警务处中央捕房的前巡佐帕特里克·J·凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）昨天下午作为申请人出庭领事法庭，起诉上海公共租界工部局。凯利声称他被非法从警队除名，并要求工部局支付约500英镑，他称这是他在养老金账户中的存款金额。
他声称，这笔款项以及代表六个月薪水的3,546美元被非法剥夺。
申请人还要求工部局支付他、他的妻子和孩子们前往英国的二等舱船费、诉讼费以及500美元。美国总领事克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）担任庭长，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦 Y.（Y. Miura，音译）协助审理。

凯利由埃利斯与海斯律师事务所（Messrs. Ellis & Hays）的H·A·里克斯先生代理，而市政律师R·T·布莱恩 junior 先生代表上海公共租界工部局出庭。领事法庭秘书E·A·朗先生也在场。
在要求凯利作证之前，里克斯先生声明，本案并非审判申请人是否犯有被指控的罪行，而是工部局在终止其雇佣关系并拿走属于他的钱财时，行为不合规范，甚至专横跋扈。
此时，布莱恩先生向法庭提交了凯利原始审判的记录、审判官的报告、市政律师的报告、申请人的个人日记以及《上海公共租界工部局警务指南与规章》。
“在一个人被证实犯有未报告没收手枪和弹药的罪行后，关键是要证明手枪和弹药确实被没收了，”里克斯先生说。“是否有手枪和弹药被没收？”他问道。

报告不准确
凯利随后宣誓，里克斯先生向法庭解释说，尽管可能会出现申请人攻击一两个人的情况，但他出庭是为了恢复自己的信誉。
申请人告诉法庭，他出生于英国卡莱尔，于1929年10月3日在伦敦受雇于上海公共租界工部局警务处。他获得了《雇佣条款》以及一份《国王规章》副本，并被告知这些规章适用于他。他在上海收到了委任书。
他于1929年11月11日开始在上海服役，委任于1931年8月通过委任书得到确认。后来，他面临四项构成违反纪律的指控。其中两项，他在技术上认罪，但并非故意犯罪。
他说，针对他的警务诉讼报告由分区警官、助理处长H.D.M·罗伯逊记录。该报告不准确，一些问答未被收录。他还说，报告中还有改动。

损失30,000美元
在他面临这些指控时，还有其他警官面临指控，其中一些人被指控勒索钱财。他被认定参与勒索并受到最严厉的惩罚。这给他造成了超过30,000美元的损失。
申请人继续说，他已婚并有两个孩子；他们已随妻子乘船前往英国。他留下来处理此案，但他打算返回英国，他曾在那里服役于本土陆军。
凯利称，没有进行初步调查，他首先在所谓的审判中接受罗伯逊先生的讯问。警队高级成员曾告诉他，罗伯逊先生无权审判他，法庭应由一名分区警官和两名督察组成。起初，当罗伯逊先生讯问他时，梅森督察在场。

搜查抽屉
他被问及是否在3月30日因一起鸦片案去过大沽路。当被问及为何未在日记中提及此次访问时，凯利回答说，他认为没有必要，因为他已在汽车日记中报告了此事。讯问结束后，他离开房间，半小时后被告知停职，他的抽屉被搜查，并被要求交出手枪和委任证。
4月11日，一份指控清单交给了他，同时交给他的还有多人作出的若干陈述。他被告知将这些陈述交给华籍巡捕阅读。
里克斯先生随后处理了针对凯利的第一项和第三项指控，即他在官方文件《第一犯罪日记》、F.I.R. 821号中 knowingly 制作并签署了虚假陈述，以及他在3月30日在中央捕房的巡捕日记本中作了虚假和不实的陈述。此时，里克斯先生指出，后一份文件不过是一份值班表。

page_data.en:
No Time to Fill In Diary
In practice, Kelly told the Court,
the instructions at the front of the
book were not carried out. There
would be no time to fill in the diary.
Many detectives made out the diary
in the same manner as he did. On
the day in questioning he had had a
poisoning and a larceny case and
had visited many places which he
had not entered in the diary. The
inspector-in-charge of the C.I.D.
at central had ticked off the entries.
Petitioner denied that he was trying
to conceal his visit to Taku Road as
he had entered it in the motor car
diary. On that day he had visited
three places in connection with a
poisoning case and others.
He explained that the first crime
diary was a document prepared by
the detectives in the force for the
Municipal Advocate with a view to
prosecution when an arrest was made.
In his case a second man had been
arrested in connection with the opium
case and it had been found that he
had no connection with the case,
therefore no entry had been made in
the first crime diary. If a case was
of no particular importance a detec-
tive wrote the main body of the re-
port and handed it to a Chinese clerk
to complete for the F.I.R.

Not Adhered to
The practice of placing the names
of places visited in the first crime
book was not adhered to by many
detectives in the force. In this case
he had been to Taku Road and had
found nothing there to warrant a
conviction of a man. Therefore, it
had not been necessary to enter the
visit in the book. He had, however,
placed therein a visit to Tsingkong
Li, off Jessfield Road when six men
were convicted in the District Court.
The first sheet of the diary, he
said, had been typed by the clerk
from information received from the
F.I.R. The possession of two ounces
of opium was, however, a trivial
offence. Here he pointed out that
he had been accused of making a
false entry in the first crime diary
when the diary had been typed by a
Chinese clerk who had guessed at the
hour at which the case had been
concluded. He admitted being techni-
cally guilty of these wrong entries.
Kelly then pointed out that a ques-
tion and answer put to him had not
been reported correctly. The ques-
tion was, he said, "Did you take
from two o'clock until six to investi-
gate this opium possession case?"
and his answer had been given as
"Yes." He had not replied in this
way, but that he had released the
prisoner at six o'clock and had been
on other cases as well.
He stated that the Municipal Ad-
vocate had put into his mouth a
certain statement at his trial. This
was that he had not thought it
strange that all the detectives, who
had gone to Taku Road, had not men-
tioned it in their diaries. He had
replied that he was not responsible
for their actions. (On this trifling
case he had been engaged for a few
minutes during the day and he had
also been investigating an attempted
suicide, the snatching of $1,000, a
shooting on Szechuen Road Bridge
and a larceny case in Kiangsi Road.
In addition there were many other
cases.

Second Charge
Mr. Reeks then stated that the
second charge had first been framed
that Kelly, without making an
official entry in the charge-room, had
released a Chinese prisoner. Later
this had been amended, when it had
been found out that it was not his
duty to make an entry, to a charge
that he had unnecessarily detained
one Chinese and had released him in
an improper manner.
page_data.zh:
无暇填写日志
凯利（Kelly）告诉法庭，实际上，
手册前面的指示并未得到执行。
根本没有时间去填写日志。
许多侦探制作日志的方式都与他相同。
在受讯问的那一天，他处理了一起
投毒案和一起盗窃案，并走访了许多
未在日志中登记的地方。中央刑事侦缉处
（C.I.D.）的主管督察已在条目上打勾核准。
申请人否认他试图隐瞒对大沽路
（Taku Road）的访问，因为他已在
汽车日志中进行了登记。在那一天，
他因一起投毒案及其他案件走访了
三个地点。

他解释说，第一份犯罪日志是警队
侦探为市政检察官准备的文件，旨在
逮捕时用于起诉。在他的案件中，另
一名男子因鸦片案被捕，但后来发现
他与该案无关，因此未在第一份犯罪
日志中进行登记。如果案件不是特别
重要，侦探会撰写报告的主要内容，
并将其交给一名华籍书记员，以完成
首份情报报告（F.I.R.）。

未予遵守
许多警队侦探并未遵守将走访地点
名称列入第一份犯罪记录簿的做法。
在此案中，他曾去过大沽路，但未发
现任何足以定罪某人的证据。因此，
没有必要在记录簿中登记此次访问。
然而，他确实登记了对杰斯菲尔德路
（Jessfield Road）附近的清江路里
（Tsingkong Li，音译）的一次访问，
当时有六名男子在地方法院被定罪。
他说，日志的第一页是由书记员根据
从首份情报报告（F.I.R.）收到的信息
打字录入的。然而，持有两盎司鸦片
属于轻微罪行。在此，他指出，他被
指控在第一份犯罪日志中做虚假登记，
而该日志实际上是由一名华籍书记员
打字录入的，该书记员猜测了案件结
束的时间。他承认在技术上对这些错
误登记负有责任。
凯利随后指出，向他提出的一个问
题及回答未被正确记录。他说，问题
是：“你是否从两点到六点调查这起
鸦片持有案？”而他的回答被记录为
“是”。他并非如此回答，而是说他
在六点钟释放了囚犯，并且当时也在
处理其他案件。

他表示，市政检察官在审判时将某
种陈述强加于他。该陈述称，他并不
觉得奇怪的是，所有去过大沽路的侦
探均未在日志中提及此事。他回答说，
他不对他们的行为负责。（在这起微
小案件中，他白天仅参与了几分钟，
此外他还调查了一起自杀未遂案、一
起1,000元抢劫案、四川路桥枪击案
以及江西路的一起盗窃案。此外还有
许多其他案件。

第二项指控
里克斯先生（Mr. Reeks）随后表示，
针对凯利的第二项指控最初拟定为：
凯利未在拘留室进行正式登记便释放
了一名中国囚犯。后来，当发现这并
非他的职责时，该指控被修改为：他
不必要地拘留了一名中国人，并以不
当方式将其释放。

page_data.en:
29161

Kelly then told the Court that in
connection with this case the First
Information Report was made out by
Sub-Ins. Darters and the fact that a
man had been arrested for being in
possession of opium should have
been entered in the report. "It was
not my duty to make the entry," he
went on.
About five o'clock that afternoon
he found that a second man had
been arrested in connection with the
case and he was about to question
this man when he was ordered to
complete another report. About
8.40 p.m. he took his wife to a whist
drive and a telephone message came
to him that the prisoner had not
been released. He thereupon went
down to the charge-room and
released the man with the assistance
of Sub-Insp. Verhovsky, who stated
that there was no entry about the
man and that it was Sub-Insp.
Darter's duty to make the entry.
At times, he said, prisoners were
released by the gatemen and Mr.
Verhovsky who was on charge-room
duty did not know for two hours
that a man was being detained. The
second man, arrested on suspicion,
Kelly stated, had not been black-
mailed. His arrest was not entered
in the crime diary as it was found
he had no connection with the case.
He admitted that his diary was
wrong by about ten minutes or so in
the times but there had been no
falsification of the entries.

Question of Missing Pistol

The fourth charge against Kelly
was that he had failed to account for
money, pistol and ammunition and
opium taken at House 7, Lane 183
Tuku Road. Kelly alleged that there
had been no pistol or ammunition
found in the house. The man ar-
rested had stated that a pistol and
ammunition had been found because
a detective had told him that a paper
parcel contained these articles. In
this case the Chinese alleged to have
been blackmailed did not give evid-
ence in the District Court where the
case was heard.
Mr. Reeks:—Kelly, had you found
a pistol and ammunition, would you
have been guilty of a serious offence?
—I should have been guilty of a
serious crime against the police force.
I should have been guilty of a cri-
minal offence. They asked me no
questions about the pistol but search-
ed my drawers before it was ever
mentioned. The only serious charge
against me is having seized a pistol
and ammunition. If I had seized it
and had failed to return it I could
have been charged with larceny.
There were no proceedings against
me. There was certainly no ammuni-
tion and pistol in that house.
Kelly then stated that during the
questioning of a Chinese lawyer in
connection with the charges, Mr.
Robertson had called the man a liar
and had threatened to have him re-
moved from the Court lawyers' roll
by using his influence with Mr. Bryan.
Mr. Robertson had also accused wit-
ness of having concocted a story by
collaborating with Chinese detectives.
Petitioner had also questioned Mr.
Verhovsky, who had not been seen
until a fortnight later by Mr. Robert-
son, about his memory for facts which
happened so long ago. He had been
stopped, however.
page_data.zh:
29161

凯利随后告诉法庭，在此案中，首
份情报报告由副督察达特斯
（Sub-Ins. Darters）填写，某人因持
有鸦片被捕的事实本应记入该报告。
“这并不是我的职责去进行登记，”
他继续说道。

当天下午五点左右，他发现另有一
人因该案被捕，他正准备讯问此人时，
却接到命令去完成另一份报告。晚上
8点40分左右，他送妻子去参加惠斯特
牌友聚会，随后接到电话留言，称该
囚犯尚未被释放。他随即前往拘留室，
在副督察韦尔霍夫斯基
（Sub-Insp. Verhovsky）的协助下释
放了该男子。韦尔霍夫斯基表示，关
于该男子没有任何登记，且进行登记
是副督察达特（Darter）的职责。

他说，有时囚犯由门卫释放，而在
拘留室值班的韦尔霍夫斯基先生在两
小时内都不知道有人被拘留。凯利表
示，因涉嫌被捕的第二名男子并未遭
到勒索。由于发现他与案件无关，其
逮捕行动未记入犯罪日志。他承认他
的日志在时间记录上有大约十分钟左
右的误差，但条目本身并无伪造。

手枪失踪问题

针对凯利的第四项指控是，他未能
说明在土库路（Tuku Road，音译）
183弄7号屋内查获的钱款、手枪、弹
药和鸦片的去向。凯利声称在屋内并
未发现手枪或弹药。被捕男子称发现
了手枪和弹药，是因为一名侦探告诉
他一个纸包裹内装有这些物品。在此
案中，据称遭到勒索的这名中国人在
审理此案的地方法院并未出庭作证。

里克斯先生问：——凯利，如果你
发现了手枪和弹药，你是否犯有严重
罪行？——我将犯下针对警队的严重
罪行。我将构成刑事犯罪。他们从未
就手枪向我提问，而是在提及此事之
前就搜查了我的抽屉。对我唯一的严
重指控是扣押了一把手枪和弹药。如
果我扣押了它而未归还，我可能会被
指控犯有盗窃罪。并没有对我提起任
何诉讼。那所房子里肯定没有弹药和
手枪。

凯利随后表示，在与指控相关的对
一名中国律师的讯问过程中，罗伯逊
先生（Mr. Robertson）称该人为骗子，
并威胁要利用他对布莱恩先生
（Mr. Bryan）的影响力，将该人从法
庭律师名册中除名。罗伯逊先生还指
控证人与华籍侦探勾结，编造故事。
申请人也曾就事实记忆问题讯问韦尔
霍夫斯基先生，毕竟事情已过去许久，
但罗伯逊先生直到两周后才见到韦尔
霍夫斯基先生。不过，这一讯问被叫
停。

page_data.en:
Case Adjourned
In connection with the extortion
charge the complainant's wife had not
implicated him in any way. Kelly
then told the Court that he had gained
six awards during his service and
had received six punishments. The
awards included a commendation for
arresting a gang of murderers while
the offences entered against him had
been committed during his first three
years in the force when he was a
young policeman. None of them
were serious.
Referring to the release of the Chi-
nese, Kelly said that this would have
been regular had Sub-Insp. Darters
entered it. Verhovsky did not enter
it as it would have made Sub-Insp.
Darters look careless. He added that
there was a certain amount of fric-
tion between the plain-clothes branch
and the uniformed men. There were
arguments between the two branches
and a certain amount of jealousy.
The hearing was then adjourned
until tomorrow at 2.30 p.m.
page_data.zh:
案件休庭
关于敲诈勒索指控，投诉人的妻子
并未以任何方式牵连他。凯利随后告
诉法庭，他在服役期间曾获得六次奖
励，并受到六次处罚。奖励包括因逮
捕一个谋杀团伙而获得的嘉奖，而记
录在案的违规行为发生在他加入警队
的前三年，当时他还是一名年轻警察。
这些违规均不严重。

谈到释放该名中国人的事，凯利说，
如果副督察达特斯进行了登记，这一
操作本是合规的。韦尔霍夫斯基未进
行登记，因为那样会使副督察达特斯
显得粗心大意。他补充说，便衣部门
与制服警员之间存在一定的摩擦。两
个部门之间存在争论和一定程度的嫉
妒。
听证会随后休庭，至明天下午2点30
分继续。

《字林西报》。
1939年10月25日
29150
前警佐
起诉
工部局
领事法庭审理涉嫌违约案及索赔逾25,000美元养老金和3,546美元薪金
凯利警佐要求洗清违规指控
埃利斯与海斯律师事务所（Messrs. Ellis and Hays）的H. A. Reeks先生昨日下午在领事法庭代表其当事人、前警佐帕特里克·J. 凯利（Patrick J. Kelly）起诉上海公共租界工部局时声明，其当事人并非出于个人报复，而是即将返回英国，希望澄清名誉。
昨日传召的唯一证人是凯利先生，整个下午的时间都用于其代理律师对他的讯问。
法庭由美国总领事克拉伦斯·E. 高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）担任主席，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）和日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）组成。
本案系前警务人员指控工部局违反雇佣合同，索赔他认为应得的超过25,000美元养老金；3,546美元，相当于代通知金的六个月薪金；以及申请人及其妻儿返回英国的二等舱船票费。听证会在工部局会议室举行。
代表被告工部局出庭的工部局法律顾问R. T. Bryan先生将在下周四下午的下一次听证会上对凯利先生进行交叉质询，案件在昨日短暂听证后延期至该日期。
“专横行为”
Reeks先生在开庭陈述中表示，凯利先生本人将是己方唯一的证人。Reeks先生指控工部局在终止凯利先生的雇佣关系并剥夺其正当所属款项时，行事违规且专横。辩护律师提交称，他将向法庭提供的证据将证明针对工部局的所谓违规行为属实，并进而宣称“工部局对他施加如此惩罚没有任何依据”。
工部局由Bryan先生向法庭提交的答辩状是对索赔的全面否认。答辩状宣称，凯利先生因“有损警队声誉的行为”而被开除出警队。答辩状随后列举了一系列据称凯利先生被认定有罪的指控，包括虚假陈述和推诿塞责，即他于去年3月30日在一份官方文件（即警方首罪日记簿）中故意制作并签署虚假陈述，涉及不光彩行为，“因为你在1939年3月30日于中央巡捕房，不必要地拘留了一名名为曾来典（Tsang Lai Dien，音译）的人，并在值班警官不知情且未同意的情况下以不当方式将其释放，从而损害了警队的声誉；”“你在3月30日于中央巡捕房，故意在你的侦探日记簿40A号中作出虚假和误导性陈述。”针对凯利先生列出的第四项指控称，他卷入腐败行为，即在去年3月30日未能

24151

Rules On Dismissal
“5.—The Rules and Regulations
governing the conduct of police
officers hereinbefore referred to
(to which petitioner will refer at
the trial for the full and correct
terms thereof) provide inter alia:
(a) In Section IV 2 thereof that in
all cases involving major punish-
ments, including dismissal, regular
proceedings shall be drawn up in
accordance with the procedure laid
down in the said regulations; (b)
That every member should have
the fullest facility for defending
himself; (c) That anyone found
guilty and ordered to be dismissed
should have a right of appeal to
the Council; and (d) There was
further an implied contract that any
proceedings should be conducted in
a fair and impartial manner and
that nothing should be done in an
arbitrary manner and in prejudice
of fairness and natural justice.”
After alleging that the Council had
committed a breach of its own
police regulations and declaring
that only a preliminary inquiry was
held into his case, the petition went
on to deal with the charges pre-
ferred against petitioner and went
on to state: “Petitioner was made
to answer these charges of a
criminal nature, being charges of
blackmail and extortion brought
against other members of the police
force.”
The petition then continues: “The
only serious charge against peti-
tioner was that under (d) of para-
graph 5 to the effect that the peti-
tioner had failed to account for
and make a true return of certain
property, to wit: money, pistol,
ammunition and opium seized. That
charge was not proceeded with
against the petitioner but a finding
on that charge was rendered after
the hearing of a fifth charge, being
a criminal charge, against three
other officers of the police force
of extorting money, with which
charge petitioner was not faced and
further upon the hearing of that
charge of extortion against other
accused no evidence transpired
against the petitioner to enable a
finding to be made against the
petitioner on the said fourth charge
made against the petitioner.
Irregular Proceedings
“The proceedings were further
irregular in that they were not
conducted in a fair and impartial
manner by the officer conducting
the inquiry as required in the ex-
ercise of powers conferred upon
him, and he wrongfully and in
breach of his duty did interfere
with witnesses in the giving of
their evidence and showed a bias
and a determination to find the
petitioner guilty of infractions of
police regulations, being infractions
committed with an alleged view to
assist in the commission of a major
crime.
“Further the notes made by the
divisional officer, while purporting
to be a verbatim rendering in
point of fact, only contained such
notes as he chose to incorporate
and omitted many of his questions
and the answers thereto.

24151

关于开除的规定
“5.—前述管理警务人员行为的规章条例（申请人将在庭审中引用其完整且正确的条款）其中包括：(a) 其中第四节第二条规定，在所有涉及重大处罚（包括开除）的案件中，应按照上述规章规定的程序制定正式诉讼文书；(b) 每位成员应拥有为自己辩护的最充分便利；(c) 任何被认定有罪并被命令开除的人应有权向工部局上诉；以及 (d) 此外还有一项默示合同，即任何诉讼程序应以公平和公正的方式进行，不得以武断方式行事或损害公平与自然正义。”
在指控工部局违反其自身的警察规章并宣称仅对其案件进行了初步调查后，诉状继续处理针对申请人提出的指控，并陈述道：“申请人被迫回答这些具有刑事性质的指控，即针对其他警务人员提出的勒索和敲诈指控。”
诉状接着写道：“针对申请人的唯一严重指控是第5段(d)项下的内容，即申请人未能说明并如实上报某些财产，即：没收的现金、手枪、弹药和鸦片。该指控并未对申请人进行追诉，但在听取针对其他三名警务人员的第五项指控（一项刑事指控，即敲诈钱财）后，对该指控作出了裁决，申请人并未面临该项指控，此外，在审理针对其他被告的敲诈指控时，并未出现针对申请人的证据，使得无法就针对申请人的上述第四项指控作出对申请人不利的裁决。
程序违规
“程序进一步存在违规之处，因为负责调查的官员未按行使赋予其权力所要求的那样，以公平和公正的方式进行调查，他错误且违背职责地干扰证人作证，并表现出偏见以及认定申请人违反警察规章的决心，这些违规行为据称是为了协助犯下重大罪行。
“此外，分区警官所做的记录虽然声称是逐字记录，但实际上仅包含他选择收录的内容，省略了许多他的提问及相应的回答。

page_data.en:
"The proceedings were further
irregular in that, though the petitioner was not charged with any
criminal offence, one comprehensive finding was made against a
number of officers who were accused of blackmail and extortion
and the petitioner was stated to have been dishonest and the finding of
the divisional officer against the petitioner in that context amounted to a
finding that petitioner had been guilty of a crime in that he had
been in collusion with the other
accused members of the force in
extortion and consequently guilty of
the crime of blackmail. The petitioner, having been found guilty by
the officer conducting the inquiry
of infractions of police rules the
respondent visited upon the petitioner condign punishment with a
finding that petitioner was dishonest
and guilty of criminal actions and
the plaintiff has had cast upon him
by the sentence of dismissal and
by the confiscation of moneys due
from the respondent to petitioner
the odium of having been in collusion with other members, since dismissed from the police force, in the
commission of the crime of blackmail and extortion of money.

Appeal To Council
"The appeal of petitioner to respondent against the sentence of dismissal and against the irregularity
of the proceedings was not fairly
attended to. There was further produced to the respondent a letter
written by the petitioner after dismissal to the Commissioner of
Police upon the request and suggestion of a senior officer which asked
for more considerate treatment under a promise of the same and as
evidence that petitioner was guilty
and had been in collusion in the
criminal extortion of money by
other members, since dismissed from
the police force. Petitioner had no
opportunity to appeal either in person or by counsel to state the petitioner's case and argue against the
unfairness and irregularity of the
proceedings."
The petition then charges the
Council with having wrongfully
dismissed Mr. Kelly in alleged
breach of his contract of employment and declared that the first
three charges levelled by the police
against petitioner were irregularly
framed while the fourth charge was
not heard.
In challenging the right of the
Council to terminate the employment of Mr. Kelly, on what he
declared to be only after an inquiry into trivial charges, counsel
declared that respondent had visited
the maximum punishment upon his
client amounting to a confiscation
of more than $25,000.

Records Of Inquiry
Before Mr. Kelly was called to
the witness-box, Mr. Bryan handed
into court records allegedly taken
by the police at the inquiry of the
case against petitioner which Mr.
Bryan explained would materially
assist the court in following the
evidence given by petitioner. The
records, Mr. Bryan said, included
the testimony of Mr. Kelly. Mr.
Reeks, having no objection, the
records were handed into court.
"If a man is found guilty of not
having made a report of a seizure
of pistols and ammunition," Mr.
Reeks interjected, "it is first necessary to prove that the ammunition
was seized whereas the evidence
which will be produced before the
court will show that there never
was any pistol or ammunition. . . .
If four witnesses say that there was
no pistol and ammunition seized
and one say there was, can you say
that Kelly was guilty of a breach
of regulations?"
page_data.zh:
“程序进一步存在违规之处，尽管申请人未被指控任何刑事犯罪，但对多名被控勒索和敲诈的警官作出了一项综合裁决，并称申请人不诚实，分区警官在此背景下对申请人作出的裁决相当于认定申请人犯有罪行，因为他与其他被控警员串通进行敲诈，因而犯有勒索罪。申请人被负责调查的官员认定违反警察规章后，被告对申请人施加了应有的惩罚，认定申请人不诚实并犯有刑事行为，原告因被开除判决以及没收被告欠申请人的款项而蒙受了与他人串通犯下勒索和敲诈钱财罪行的恶名，这些人此后也被开除出警队。

向工部局上诉
“申请人就开除判决及程序违规向被告提出的上诉未得到公正处理。此外，向被告出示了一封申请人在开除后应一名高级警官的要求和建议写给警务处长的信，信中承诺给予更体贴的待遇，并以此作为申请人有罪并与其他已被开除出警队的成员串通进行刑事敲诈钱财的证据。申请人没有机会亲自或通过律师陈述案情，并就程序的不公和违规进行辩论。”
诉状随后指控工部局涉嫌违反雇佣合同错误地开除了凯利先生，并宣称警方针对申请人提出的前三项指控起草违规，而第四项指控未经审理。
在质疑工部局终止凯利先生雇佣关系的权利时，辩护律师宣称这仅仅是在对琐碎指控进行调查之后进行的，并指出被告对其当事人施加了最高惩罚，相当于没收超过25,000美元。

调查记录
在凯利先生被传唤至证人席之前，Bryan先生向法庭提交了据称由警方在针对申请人的案件调查中取得的记录，Bryan先生解释说这将极大地帮助法庭跟进申请人提供的证据。Bryan先生称，这些记录包括凯利先生的证词。由于Reeks先生没有异议，记录被提交法庭。
“如果一个人因未报告缴获手枪和弹药而被认定有罪，”Reeks先生插话道，“首先必须证明弹药确实被缴获，而将在法庭上出示的证据将显示根本没有任何手枪或弹药……如果有四名证人说没有缴获手枪和弹药，而一人说有，你能说凯利违反了规章吗？”

page_data.en:
Mr. Reeks pointed out that it
might transpire from the testimony
that petitioner was making an
attack against one or two members
of the police force, going on to
explain that this was inevitable
perhaps in such a case, explaining
however, that his client was not
animated by a motive of revenge
against anyone.
Mr. Kelly's Evidence
Mr. Kelly then entered the
witness-box and, after giving details
of the circumstances attending his
employment by the Council, stated
that the four charges preferred
against him by the police force had
been amended to charges of breach-
es of discipline in the force. He
pleaded technical, but not wilful
and intentional, guilt to one of the
breaches alleged.
Witness declared, in reply to his
counsel, that the report of the pro-
ceedings before the police inquiring
officer was inaccurate, some ques-
tions and answers were omitted and
others had been altered. Six police
officers, he said, were involved in
the investigation and were adjudged
guilty of extortion.
Stayed To Fight
Declaring that the punishment
meted out to him was most severe
and involved a loss of $30,000 to
him, witness said he was married
with two children, whom he said
had returned to England while he
stayed behind to "fight this case."
It was his intention to rejoin them
after. He was in the Territorial
Army in England, witness said. He
explained that the superannuation
fund belongs to an employee of the
Council and is in the nature of
deferred pay for his services.
Witness then said he was tried by
a superior officer and he was
suspended from duty from April 1
to 13 last. He went on to say that
he conversed with senior officers of
the force and gathered that the
officer in question had no authority
to try him. He went on to relate
that he was suspended from duty,
and that his desk was searched.
Handing the court a book, Mr.
Reeks then said: "I ask Your
Honours to look at this so-called
diary and to see from the marks of
internal evidence if it is not borne
out that it is only a duty roster
showing on what duty a man has
been engaged, showing where and
what he has been doing." Mr.
Reeks then pointed out that the first
page contained instructions which
witness later explained were not
carried out in practice. Witness, in
reply to a long examination by his
counsel, said that certain statements
in the roster were not absolutely
correct.
Counsel caused some surprise
when he asked witness whether the
Municipal Advocate had not put a
certain statement into his mouth at
his trial.
"Were you put that question and
did you answer it in that manner?"
counsel asked, to which witness
replied: "That was not my answer.
I answered that I was not respon-
sible for the actions of other
people."

里克斯（Reeks）先生指出，从证词中可能会显现出，原告正在对警队的一两名成员发起攻击，他接着解释说，在这种情况下这或许是不可避免的，但他同时说明，他的委托人并非出于对任何人的报复动机。

凯利先生的证词
凯利先生随后进入证人席，在详细陈述了受雇于工部局的相关情况后表示，警队对他提出的四项指控已修改为违反警队纪律的指控。他就其中一项被指控的违纪行为承认技术性过失，但否认是故意和蓄意为之。

证人在回答其辩护律师的提问时声明，警务调查官员所记录的诉讼程序报告不准确，部分问答被遗漏，其他内容则被篡改。他说，共有六名警官卷入该调查，并被裁定犯有勒索罪。

坚持抗争
证人表示，对他施加的惩罚极为严厉，导致他损失了30,000美元。他说自己已婚并育有两个孩子，孩子们已返回英国，而他则留下来“为此案抗争”。他打算事后与他们团聚。证人称，他曾在英国的本土陆军（Territorial Army）服役。他解释说，养老金基金属于工部局雇员所有，性质上为其服务提供的延期支付薪酬。

证人随后表示，他由一名上级军官进行审判，并于去年4月1日至13日被停职。他接着说，他与警队的高级官员进行了交谈，并获悉涉事官员无权审判他。他继续叙述道，他被停职，且他的办公桌受到了搜查。

里克斯先生向法庭递交了一本册子，随后说道：“我请诸位法官阁下查阅这本所谓的日记，并从其内在证据的痕迹来看，它是否仅仅是一份值班表，显示某人从事何种勤务，以及他在何处、做了何事。”里克斯先生随后指出，第一页包含一些指令，而证人后来解释称这些指令在实践中并未执行。证人在回答其辩护律师的长时间讯问时表示，值班表中的某些陈述并不完全正确。

当辩护律师询问证人，市政检察官是否在审判时诱导他说出某项特定陈述时，引起了一些惊讶。

“你是否被问及该问题，并以那种方式作了回答？”辩护律师问道，证人回答说：“那不是我的回答。我回答的是，我对其他人的行为不负责任。”

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

OCT 20 1939

SMC Sued
By Former
Policeman

£500, Compensation
Passage Money
Demanded

HEARING SET
FOR TUESDAY

Dismissal Of P.J. Kelly
From SMP Claimed
Wrongful

The Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil will appear as defendants in an
action which will be brought be-
fore the Court of Consuls next
Tuesday by Mr. Patrick John Kel-
ley, former Sergeant of the Settle-
ment police force, charging
wrongful dismissal from the
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Judges at the hearing will be
Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, American
Consul-General and presiding
judge of the Court of Consuls, Sir
Herbert Phillips, British Consul-
General, and Mr. Y. Miura,
Japanese Consul-General.
Five Hundred Pounds
The plaintiff was dismissed from
the Municipal Police toward the
beginning of this year, following
an enquiry conducted into his be-
havior by the SMP.
An amount of £500 is involved
in the suit, plaintiff asking for
the sum mentioned as compensa-
tion, while an additional sum for
passage to England is also being
sought by the plaintiff from the
Council. The plaintiff is being
represented in the action by Messrs
Ellis and Have.
Previous Cases
It has been some time since any
hearings have been held before
the Court of Consuls. The last
case involved Mr. S. H. Loh who
prosecuted the Shanghai Municipal
Council after his wife had alleged-
ly been ill-treated by a member
of the SMP, when some trouble
arose over road widening at Race
Course Road last year.
Hose Coupling
In January, 1937, the Municipal
Council lost a suit brought before
the Court by Mrs. Schneider, who
had been injured in the eye when
Settlement firemen held a practise
close to the Race Course apart-
ments, and one of the hose coup-
lings on a fire ladder broke and
injured the lady.
Another case which created a
great amount of interest, happen-
ed during the latter part of 1936,
when the SMC was sued by a
group of Chinese, after an auto-
mobile carrying five persons top-
pled over the Point Island bridge.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》

1939年10月20日

前警察起诉
上海公共租界工部局

索赔500英镑
及回国船费

听证会定于
周二举行

声称P.J.凯利
被上海公共租界巡捕房
非法解雇

上海公共租界工部局将作为被告，出庭应对下周二由前公共租界巡捕房警长帕特里克·约翰·凯利（Patrick John Kelley）先生在领事法庭提起的诉讼，指控上海公共租界巡捕房将其非法解雇。

听证会的法官将是美国总领事兼领事法庭主审法官克拉伦斯·E·高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）先生、英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯（Herbert Phillips）爵士，以及日本总领事三浦（Y. Miura）先生。

五百英镑
原告于今年年初被公共租界巡捕房解雇，此前巡捕房对其行为进行了调查。

本案涉及金额为500英镑，原告要求将该金额作为赔偿，同时原告还向工部局索要额外的回国船费。原告在本案中由埃利斯（Ellis）和黑夫（Have）律师事务所代理。

既往案例
领事法庭已有段时间未举行听证会。上一个案件涉及罗（S. H. Loh）先生，他在去年跑马厅路（Race Course Road）拓宽工程引发纠纷期间，其妻子据称遭到一名巡捕房成员的虐待，随后他起诉了上海公共租界工部局。

消防水带接口
1937年1月，工部局在一起由施奈德（Schneider）夫人提起的诉讼中败诉。当时，公共租界消防员在靠近跑马厅公寓的地方进行演习，消防梯上的一个水带接口断裂，致使施奈德夫人眼部受伤。

另一起引起极大关注的案件发生在1936年下半年，当时一辆载有五人的汽车翻越外白渡桥（Point Island bridge），一群华人因此起诉了上海公共租界工部局。
